Companion to the round-2 design review of issue #4525

Verification votes and corrections, round 2

Every new finding on the round-2 review page was put to three verifiers who tried to refute it (a source-truth lens, a design-text-fairness lens, an intent lens). This page holds their reasons and corrections verbatim. A finding survived when at least two of the three could not refute it. Rejected candidates are listed at the end. The disposition rows of section 3 (one checker plus two re-graders per round-1 finding) are here too, under dispo-F.. and dispo-C.. anchors. The round-1 votes are on their own page.

Design text checked: design.txt:51 "The problem is that a bare bf16* pointer does not identify the cache layout. [Saved review text]"; :22 "VNNI, native K, packed V, blocked packed K | ... Native K stores one token's dimensions consecutively. Checker assessment: Round-1 F20 (note) asked for one scope bullet in issue #4525 restating the three constraints from Ben's comment 5765866077: the arena constructs the typed storage (no cast of the existing SIMD array), the packed view has no public pointer constructor, data() or pointer conversion, and no clearing is added to hot allocation paths. The revision keeps all three constraints in the design (lines 222, 320-337) and explicitly defers the public issue edit (lines 472, 481). We should not obtain typed storage by casting an existing SIMD array to vnni_tensor*"; "The private constructor prevents routine callers from relabelling an arbitrary row-major pointer as packed data ... There is no data(), pointer conversion"; "must not remove V's zero-initialization invariant or add implicit clearing to hot allocation paths"); the design's lines 222, 328-329 and 334 match each sentence. The live issue (facts-r2.md:25) is unchanged, which the revision states truthfully. Deferring a note-level public-record edit to separate work is acceptable; the implementing agent gets the constraints from the design.

Partly F08. Packed-V slices and iteration specified without any caller (round-1 grade Major)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: checker: Partly, source: Partly, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design.txt:63 "Limit the parent: expression reads and existing row operations. Defer slices, iteration, generic expression assignment, and expression constructors until a caller needs them." design.txt:85 "Is the smaller parent scope sufficient? | Yes. Include expression reads and typed bulk operations; defer the general tensor write and slice interfaces." design.txt:275-277 "Explicitly deferred. No packed slices or iterators; no generic row.set, set_pair, matrix.set, or owner expression constructor/assignment; no runtime shapes or general transpose interface. Leave h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp unchanged. Existing ordinary tensors may still be constructed from a packed view's read expressions. This scope decision removes the unneeded odd-boundary slice-write and temporary-slice lifetime questions." design.txt:352 step 1 "... No change to slice.hpp." design.txt:211 "v_vnni_view<T,R,D> inherits expr<view_type,R,D>. v_vnni_row<T,D> inherits expr<row_type,D>." design.txt:466 disposition "F08 F34 F37 | Scope reduced explicitly | Defer slices, iteration, generic assignment, and owner expression construction. The owner is not an expression. No shared slice-header change." The verification table at design.txt:393-401 has no row about slice lifetime.

Checker assessment: The round-1 RECOMMENDATION asked to replace the slice subsection with a one-sentence deferral, leave h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp untouched, drop the verification row "How long slices remain valid", and keep the cheap parts of the type family. The revision does all of this: slices and iterators are deferred unconditionally (design.txt:63, 277), slice.hpp is left unchanged (277, 352), the slice verification row is gone (393-401), and every KEEP item of the round-1 scope table is present (rank-2 expr base 211; row chunk/bf16_chunk 220-221; append_v_row/load_row/copy_token/copy_plane 229-244; page::v_tensor and removal of v_data/v_base 255; typed V and K kernel parameters 260-266; negative-compile checks 397; no accessor by storage offset 256; no scratch-view type 242; no page::k_tensor 251). What is missing is the caveat that all three round-1 verifiers added: the existing generic slice overload operator()(expr<B, in_d0, in_d1> const& v_in, ...) [h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp:147-177 @f46e48bab498, file unchanged through 2880c3aa9b (empty git diff)] accepts any rank-2 expr, so it binds v_vnni_view through its expr base with no edit to slice.hpp, and it captures v_in by reference (slice.hpp:168-169 "It's critical that v_in be captured by reference here"). Its result is a slice_expr over the row's chunk()/bf16_chunk() [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:695-732 @2880c3aa9b], which the design's row provides (220-221), so the path compiles. The Owner& overload [slice.hpp:38-42] forwards owner.as_view() into that same path. The design does not name this path or its rule ("do not pass a temporary"), and does not state the choice the verifiers asked for (leave the generic path as is, or add one deleted overload). Substance met, caveat missing, so partly.

Still needed: Add one sentence to "Explicitly deferred" (design.txt:277): "The existing generic expression slice [h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp:147-177] already accepts an lvalue packed view through its rank-2 expr base and captures it by reference; do not pass a temporary view, or a temporary owner through the Owner& overload at slice.hpp:38-42, to slice<>. This design leaves that path as is and adds no deleted overload." Then narrow the last sentence of 277 to "This scope decision removes the odd-boundary slice-write question and the lifetime questions of the design's own slice type."

source re-grader (Partly): The round-1 substance is done. design.txt:63 defers "slices, iteration, generic expression assignment, and expression constructors"; design.txt:277 says "No packed slices or iterators ... Leave h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp unchanged"; step 1 at design.txt:352 repeats "No change to slice.hpp"; the verification table at design.txt:393-401 has no slice-lifetime row; the KEEP items of the round-1 scope table are present (rank-2 expr base at 211, row chunk and bf16_chunk at 220-221, append_v_row/load_row/copy_token/copy_plane at 229-244, page::v_tensor and removal of v_data/v_base at 255, typed kernel parameters at 260-266, negative-compile checks at 397). What is missing is the caveat all three round-1 verifiers added (r1-findings.md F08 entries: "either leave the generic expr path as is or add one constraint, and name the choice" and "do not pass a temporary to it"). I re-derived the path from source. h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp is byte-identical between f46e48bab498 and 2880c3aa9b (empty git diff). Its overload at slice.hpp:147-150 takes expr<B, in_d0, in_d1> const& v_in with requires(d0 != DYN_SIZE && sizeof...(ds) == 1); template argument deduction accepts a derived class, and design.txt:211 makes v_vnni_view inherit expr<view_type,R,D>, so slice<R2,C2>()(packed_view, r, c) compiles with no edit to slice.hpp. slice.hpp:168-169 captures &v_in by reference ("It's critical that v_in be captured by reference here"). The result is a lambda_expr of slice_expr [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:693-732 @2880c3aa9b], which only needs the row's chunk/bf16_chunk/fp16_chunk, all of which design.txt:220-221 provide. The design does not tell the implementer this path exists, does not state the temporary rule, and its sentence at design.txt:277 "This scope decision removes the unneeded odd-boundary slice-write and temporary-slice lifetime questions" is wrong for this generic path. So: substance met, caveat missing, one misleading sentence. Partly is the right grade. Correction: The checker's residual understates the hazard. The Owner& overload at slice.hpp:38-42 is requires requires(Owner& owner) { owner.as_view(); } and forwards (*this)(owner.as_view(), offset0, offsets...). For the new owner, owner.as_view() is a prvalue v_vnni_view. That prvalue matches none of the by-value view/const_view overloads (slice.hpp:53, :90) or the const_views overload (:125), because design.txt:213 says the view does not inherit views<> and design.txt:222 gives it no pointer conversion; the only viable overload is the expr const& one at :147, which binds the temporary and captures it by reference. The temporary dies at the end of the return statement inside the Owner& overload, so slice<R2,C2>()(owner, r, c) returns a dangling expression for an LVALUE owner as well, not only for a temporary owner. Every existing as_view() in tron returns a tron::view or const_view (h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:71,75; h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:1037,1042 aligned_vector; h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:223,227 @2880c3aa9b), which matches the by-value view overloads, so no existing owner has this trap; v_vnni_tensor would be the first. design.txt:397 "Reject ... rvalue-owner views" does not cover an lvalue owner passed to slice<>. Kind: (d) omission plus (a) an inaccurate sentence at 277. Severity: minor, not note, because the design asserts the lifetime question is removed while its own owner/view pair creates a new instance of it; it stays latent because no caller at 2880c3aa9b slices a cache plane (the 39 slice<> sites in h/ and src/ slice activations, weights or scratch: ptensor.hpp:120-445, feed_forward.hpp:895-899, model.hpp:2768,2835,3042,3048, self_attention.hpp:303-362,870,1789, llama.hpp:920,1012,1347-1348). Suggested replacement for the last sentence of design.txt:277: "The existing generic expression slice [h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp:147-177] already accepts a rank-2 packed view through its expr base and captures the argument by reference. Slice only a named lvalue view. Do not pass a temporary view (for example page::v_tensor(...) written inline), and do not pass the owner: the Owner& overload at slice.hpp:38-42 forwards owner.as_view() as a temporary, so its result dangles for any owner. This design leaves slice.hpp unchanged and adds no deleted overload. The odd-boundary slice-write question is removed because no packed slice can write."

fairness re-grader (Partly): The round-1 recommendation (defer slices with one sentence, do not touch h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp, drop the verification row "How long slices remain valid", keep the cheap parts of the type family) is met in substance. Slices and iterators are deferred unconditionally [design.txt:63 "Defer slices, iteration, generic expression assignment, and expression constructors until a caller needs them"; :85; :277 "No packed slices or iterators ... Leave h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp unchanged"; :352 step 1 "No change to slice.hpp"]. The verification table [design.txt:393-401] has no slice row. Every KEEP item is present: rank-2 expr base [:211], row chunk() and bf16_chunk() [:220-221], append_v_row / load_row / copy_token / copy_plane [:232-244], page::v_tensor and removal of v_data and v_base [:255], typed K and V kernel parameters [:260-266], negative-compile checks [:397], no accessor by storage offset [:256], no scratch-view type [:242], no page::k_tensor [:251], row-major V overload as a thin forwarder [:245]. What is missing is the caveat the round-1 verifiers added: name whether the existing generic slice path stays or is blocked, and warn about its by-reference capture. I verified the path in the source. slice.hpp is byte-identical from f46e48bab498 to 2880c3aa9b (empty git diff). The generic overload operator()(expr<B, in_d0, in_d1> const& v_in, size_t offset0, Offsets...) [h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp:147-177 @f46e48bab498] accepts any rank-2 expr, so it binds v_vnni_view (the design's packed V view, which inherits expr<view_type,R,D> per design.txt:211) through its base, and it captures v_in by reference [slice.hpp:168-169 "It's critical that v_in be captured by reference here"] into a lambda_expr that stores the lambda by value [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:69-79 @2880c3aa9b]. The result is a slice_expr over the row's chunk()/bf16_chunk()/fp16_chunk() [expr.hpp:695-732 @2880c3aa9b], which the design's row provides (fp16_chunk falls back through the expr base at expr.hpp:61-66). The design names none of this, and its sentence at design.txt:277 "This scope decision removes the unneeded odd-boundary slice-write and temporary-slice lifetime questions" is over-broad relative to that path. Substance met, one concrete caveat missing, so partly. Correction: The checker's residual understates the hazard. It says "do not pass a temporary view, or a temporary owner through the Owner& overload". The Owner& overload [h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp:38-42 @f46e48bab498: requires requires(Owner& owner) { owner.as_view(); } auto operator()(Owner& owner, ...) { return (*this)(owner.as_view(), offset0, offsets...); }] forwards owner.as_view() as a prvalue. For the packed owner that prvalue is a v_vnni_view, which is not a view<> (the by-value view overload at slice.hpp:44-79 does not match) and does not inherit views<> (design.txt:213), so overload resolution selects the generic expr const& overload, which captures a reference to the temporary view. That temporary dies when the Owner& overload returns. So slice<R, D>()(packed_owner, r, c) returns a dangling reference even for an LVALUE owner, not only for a temporary owner. Existing owners are safe only because their as_view() returns a view<>, which the view overload copies by value with no reference capture. Corrected residual sentence for design.txt:277: "The existing generic expression slice [h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp:147-177] accepts an lvalue packed view through its rank-2 expr base and captures it by reference. Pass only an lvalue packed view to slice<>; never a temporary view, and never the owner itself, because the Owner& overload at slice.hpp:38-42 forwards a temporary view into that same path. This design leaves slice.hpp as is and adds no deleted overload." Then narrow the last sentence of :277 to the design's own slice type. New-defect severity: minor rather than note, because the revision removed the original design's deleted rvalue-owner slice overload and now claims the lifetime questions are gone, while the verified code path dangles for the plain owner spelling; risk stays low because no caller at main or in PR 4424 slices a cache plane (round-1 F08 evidence).

Partly F12. Arena construction pass under-specified: form, enumeration, check method (round-1 grade Major)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: checker: Partly, source: Resolved, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design.txt:324-326: "// Default-initialize the array at its allocated address. // No parentheses or braces after the array bound. ::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[block_count];" design.txt:329: "Do not use std::construct_at(p), T(), or T{} here. For the proposed trivial owner they value-initialize and clear storage." design.txt:330: "Run the construction helper in book::allocate_kv_group after installing a successful allocation, before publishing access. Both initial allocation and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage use this path. Preserve the early return for zero-byte arenas." design.txt:331: "For uniform geometry, construct one array over the just-allocated arena's complete contiguous block region. Its bound is the checked arena byte count divided by sizeof(kv_block_t). This matches the existing uniform accessor's indexing across slots." design.txt:332: "For heterogeneous geometry, enumerate physical storage offsets once and select only slots in the just-allocated arena. Restoring the reclaimable arena must not restart objects in the retained arena. ... layout_t::storage_location identifies its arena; slot_base gives arena + n_pages * byte_offset. Construct geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks at that address." design.txt:333: "Include the physical EAGLE KV slot once, with the primary geometry. Do not touch x_data, the separate EAGLE embedding buffer; it contains no KV blocks. Construction cannot rely solely on the logical active-slot loop, which omits that extra physical slot." design.txt:337: "Verify the construction form with the pinned compiler. Check the optimized allocation/restore paths for no memory-clearing loop or call." design.txt:399: "Check block size/offset/alignment contracts and trivial type traits. Verify construction adds no clear operation in optimized code." design.txt:468 (section 9): "F12 F40 F56 C01 C09 | Accepted; array extent clarified | Default-initialize actual block arrays. One array per uniform arena; one per heterogeneous physical slot. Include EAGLE KV, exclude embeddings."

Checker assessment: Round 1 (as narrowed by the verifiers) asked for four things: (a) the exact construction spelling with no parentheses or braces, (b) an explicit ban on std::construct_at(p), T() and T{} as value-initialization, (c) the call sites book::allocate_kv_group and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage named in prose, and (d) an executable check for unwanted clearing, plus the refinement that construction runs once per slot region and that the EAGLE region exists only under uniform geometry. Items (a), (b) and (c) are met exactly (design.txt:324-330). The enumeration is right and verified: retained/reclaimable bytes are n_pages times the sum over slots of n_kv_heads * (2 * 64 * head_size * 2) bytes [kv_cache.hpp:651-668, 1160-1166 @2880c3aa9b], so under uniform geometry the arena is an exact multiple of sizeof(kv_block_t) and the whole-arena array bound is correct; the uniform accessor indexes blocks[(slot.i * n_kv_heads + kv_head) * n_pages + pg] from one base [kv_cache.hpp:1283-1284], which the whole-arena array matches; storage_location and slot_base are described correctly [kv_cache.hpp:727-736, 1188-1198]; the zero-byte early return exists [kv_cache.hpp:1200]; restore allocates only the reclaimable arena [kv_cache.hpp:963-974]. The EAGLE bullet (design.txt:333) is accurate but incomplete: the EAGLE physical slot exists only when eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0 [kv_cache.hpp:771] and calculate_allocation_sizes returns nullopt otherwise [kv_cache.hpp:1157-1158]; it lives in the retained arena after the active retained prefix [kv_cache.hpp:716-718, 733-735], so the uniform whole-arena array already covers it, and the heterogeneous path never has one. The bullet does not say this, so an implementer may add a dead EAGLE branch to the heterogeneous enumeration. Item (d) was met by a different means: the type-trait-only check was replaced by inspection of the optimized allocation/restore paths for memset or clearing loops (design.txt:337, 399, 441). That detects the failure mode but is a manual disassembly step rather than the executable poison-fill test the verifier asked for. The tensor.hpp:263 construct_at precedent warning is absent; the explicit ban at :329 covers its practical effect. Note, not a defect: the array form places element 0 at region_base without an array cookie only because kv_block_t is trivially destructible (Itanium ABI cookie rule), which design.txt:328 already requires.

Still needed: (1) In design.txt:333 add: "The EAGLE KV slot exists only under uniform geometry (eagle_compatible requires layout_t::uniform_geometry, kv_cache.hpp:771) and lies in the retained arena after the active retained prefix, so the uniform whole-arena array already includes it; the heterogeneous path has no EAGLE slot." (2) Optional: in design.txt:399 add an executable check: "Add a t_llama_unit case that fills a 64-byte-aligned buffer with a poison byte, runs the chosen construction form over it, and requires every byte unchanged; the trivial-type traits cannot detect value-initialization."

source re-grader (Resolved): The narrowed round-1 asks were: (a) the exact construction spelling with no parentheses or braces, (b) a ban on std::construct_at(p), T() and T{}, (c) the call sites book::allocate_kv_group and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage named in prose, (d) a check that can detect unwanted clearing, plus the refinement that construction runs once per slot region under heterogeneous geometry. (a) is met verbatim: "::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[block_count];" with the comment "No parentheses or braces after the array bound" [design.txt:324-326]. (b) is met: "Do not use std::construct_at(p), T(), or T{} here. For the proposed trivial owner they value-initialize and clear storage" [design.txt:329]. (c) is met: "Run the construction helper in book::allocate_kv_group after installing a successful allocation, before publishing access. Both initial allocation and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage use this path. Preserve the early return for zero-byte arenas" [design.txt:330]; source agrees: allocate_kv_group(reclaimable, bytes) returns early on bytes == 0 and installs the arena with destination.emplace [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1199-1208@2880c3aa9b], the constructor calls it for retained then reclaimable [kv_cache.hpp:1101-1102] and publishes later via refresh_kv_blocks_alias [kv_cache.hpp:1114, 1222-1228], and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage goes through the same function [kv_cache.hpp:968]. The enumeration is correct: under uniform geometry every slot's block size equals sizeof(kv_block_t) [kv_cache.hpp:651-668, 1316-1318], arena bytes are n_pages times the slot sum [kv_cache.hpp:1161-1167], so "checked arena byte count divided by sizeof(kv_block_t)" [design.txt:331] is an exact block count; the uniform accessor indexes one contiguous block array blocks[(slot.i * n_kv_heads + kv_head) * n_pages + pg] [kv_cache.hpp:1288-1289]; the heterogeneous accessor indexes blocks[kv_head * n_pages + pg] from slot_base(offset) [kv_cache.hpp:1331-1334], which matches "Construct geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks at that address" [design.txt:332]; storage_location and slot_base are described correctly [kv_cache.hpp:727-735, 1188-1197]. (d) is met by a different means: "Check the optimized allocation/restore paths for no memory-clearing loop or call" [design.txt:337], "Verify construction adds no clear operation in optimized code" [design.txt:399], and the objdump procedure that names "arena allocation/restore" call sites and checks for "memset ... and arena clears" [design.txt:440-441]. This detects the failure mode the verifier feared (a value-initializing form compiles to a memset or a store loop over the arena). The EAGLE bullet [design.txt:333] is accurate; the uniform whole-arena array already covers the EAGLE slot because it lives in the retained arena after the active retained prefix [kv_cache.hpp:717-719, 726-735] and EAGLE requires uniform geometry [kv_cache.hpp:771, 1158], so the prescribed enumeration builds the right thing in both cases. Section 9 records the id [design.txt:468]. Correction: Downgrade the checker's two residuals from defects to optional clarifications; the status is resolved. (1) EAGLE: the design's uniform rule (whole-arena array, design.txt:331) already includes the EAGLE slot, and the heterogeneous enumeration over physical storage offsets in the just-allocated arena never meets an EAGLE slot because calculate_allocation_sizes returns nullopt for support_eagle without uniform geometry [kv_cache.hpp:1158@2880c3aa9b] and storage_slot_count_ then equals the logical count [kv_cache.hpp:920-921]; adding "the EAGLE slot exists only under uniform geometry" is a one-clause clarity gain, not missing guidance. (2) Executable check: the revision chose a concrete disassembly check instead of the verifier's example poison-fill test; that is an acceptable design decision, and it is formally safer, because reading the bytes of a default-initialized (indeterminate) kv_block_t and comparing them is undefined behavior in C++23 except in the narrow unsigned-char cases of [basic.indet]/2, so a compiler may fold such a REQUIRE. (3) Citation precisions: the uniform accessor's indexing is at kv_cache.hpp:1288-1289 (1283-1284 are the bounds asserts); the design's array form compiles for the over-aligned kv_block_t because overload resolution first tries operator new[](size_t, align_val_t, void*), finds none, then drops the alignment argument and selects the library operator new[](size_t, void*) ([expr.new]/20), and that non-allocating form is guaranteed to pass exactly n * sizeof(T) with no array overhead ([expr.new]/16, CWG 2382), independent of the Itanium ABI trivial-destructor cookie rule the checker cited.

fairness re-grader (Partly): Round-1, as narrowed by the verifiers, asked for: (a) the exact construction spelling with no parentheses or braces, (b) an explicit ban on std::construct_at(p), T() and T{} as value-initialization, (c) the call sites book::allocate_kv_group and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage named in prose, (d) a check that can detect a zeroing construction, plus the refinements that construction runs once per slot region under heterogeneous geometry and that the EAGLE region exists only under uniform geometry. Items (a), (b) and (c) are met exactly: "::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[block_count];" with "No parentheses or braces after the array bound" [design.txt:324-326]; "Do not use std::construct_at(p), T(), or T{} here. For the proposed trivial owner they value-initialize and clear storage" [design.txt:329]; "Run the construction helper in book::allocate_kv_group after installing a successful allocation, before publishing access. Both initial allocation and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage use this path. Preserve the early return for zero-byte arenas" [design.txt:330]. I verified the enumeration against live main 2880c3aa9b (kv_cache.hpp is unchanged since c7844ca2ce). Arena bytes are n_pages times the sum over slots of n_kv_heads * (2 * 64 * head_size * 2) bytes [kv_cache.hpp:651-668, 1160-1166], so under uniform geometry the arena is an exact multiple of sizeof(kv_block_t) and the whole-arena bound at design.txt:331 is right. The uniform accessor indexes blocks[(slot.i * n_kv_heads + kv_head) * n_pages + pg] from one base [kv_cache.hpp:1288-1289], which one whole-arena array matches. storage_location and slot_base behave as the design says [kv_cache.hpp:727-736, 1188-1198]. The zero-byte early return exists [kv_cache.hpp:1200]. Restore allocates only the reclaimable arena [kv_cache.hpp:963-974]. The design's "logical active-slot loop" is for_each_active_slot, which skips slots at or beyond logical_slot_count() [kv_cache.hpp:1243-1249], so the sentence at design.txt:333 is accurate. Two gaps remain. First, the EAGLE bullet [design.txt:333] does not say that the EAGLE KV slot exists only under uniform geometry (eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0 [kv_cache.hpp:771]; calculate_allocation_sizes returns nullopt otherwise [kv_cache.hpp:1157-1158]) and lies in the retained arena after the active retained prefix [kv_cache.hpp:716-718, 726], so the uniform whole-arena array already covers it and the heterogeneous path never has one. An implementer may add a dead EAGLE branch to the heterogeneous enumeration, or a redundant second construction under uniform geometry. Kind (c) ambiguity, severity minor: neither mistake builds the wrong thing. Second, the tensor.hpp:263 construct_at precedent warning is absent; the explicit ban at design.txt:329 covers its practical effect. Item (d) is met by a different means: the design requires inspecting the optimized allocation/restore paths for clearing loops or calls [design.txt:337, 399, 441-442]. That detects value-initialization, so I count it as met in substance. Correction: Two corrections to the checker. (1) The citation for the uniform accessor indexing is kv_cache.hpp:1288-1289 @2880c3aa9b, not 1283-1284. (2) Residual (2), the executable poison-fill test, should be dropped rather than offered as optional. A test that fills a buffer, runs the placement-new form over it and requires every byte unchanged asserts the spelling of a construction expression, which the repository test policy discourages: "Do not add tautologies ... assert private implementation details ... test language or framework behavior" [AGENTS.md:39-43 @2880c3aa9b]. The design's disassembly check on the real allocation and restore paths [design.txt:337, 399, 441-442] detects the same failure (a memset or store loop) on the production path and is the acceptable substitute. Residual (1) stands as written.

Partly C01. 'Extra EAGLE region' names two different buffers; only one holds kv_blocks (round-1 grade Minor)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: checker: Partly, source: Partly, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design.txt:28 (Words row, UNCHANGED from round 1): "book, arena, EAGLE — book owns cache pages and their memory allocations. An arena is one allocated memory region. EAGLE is the speculative model with an additional cache storage region." design.txt:322: "book keeps ownership of the retained and reclaimable byte arenas. A kv_block still contains K followed by V for one head and page." design.txt:331: "For uniform geometry, construct one array over the just-allocated arena's complete contiguous block region. Its bound is the checked arena byte count divided by sizeof(kv_block_t)." design.txt:332: "For heterogeneous geometry, enumerate physical storage offsets once and select only slots in the just-allocated arena. Restoring the reclaimable arena must not restart objects in the retained arena." design.txt:333: "Include the physical EAGLE KV slot once, with the primary geometry. Do not touch x_data, the separate EAGLE embedding buffer; it contains no KV blocks. Construction cannot rely solely on the logical active-slot loop, which omits that extra physical slot. [C01] [C09]" design.txt:353 (step 2): "Check byte sizes, alignment, EAGLE storage, all geometries, and allocation failure." design.txt:468 (section 9): "F12 F40 F56 C01 C09 — Accepted; array extent clarified — ... Include EAGLE KV, exclude embeddings."

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked for four things: (1) name the two EAGLE extras separately (one extra KV storage slot with the primary geometry at the end of the retained arena, and the embedding buffer x_data that holds no kv_block); (2) say that EAGLE requires uniform geometry, so the per-arena one-array construction already covers the extra slot; (3) say that restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena, so the EAGLE slot is constructed once, in the constructor; (4) rewrite the Words row and add a clause about x_data to the 'both byte arenas' sentence (verifier narrowed: 'arena' is the code's word for the two KV regions, so only add the clause). What the revision did, checked against kv_cache.hpp at live main 2880c3aa9b (file identical from c7844ca2ce through 2880c3aa9b): - (1) is met in substance at design.txt:333. The EAGLE KV slot is a physical slot with the primary geometry [kv_cache.hpp:906-909 eagle_storage_offset() = kv_storage_offset(logical_slot_count()); :1326-1329 asserts geometry == layout_t::primary_geometry]. x_data is a separate DMA buffer holding embeddings, not kv_blocks [kv_cache.hpp:1131 std::optional<hardware::unique_dma<uint8_t[]>> x_data;, :1106-1113 allocated separately from the two arenas, :810-812 'Retained KV, reclaimable KV, and EAGLE embeddings are separate buffers']. The clause 'the logical active-slot loop ... omits that extra physical slot' is right: for_each_active_slot runs only slot < logical_slot_count() [kv_cache.hpp:1242-1249]. - (4) is met: 'both byte arenas' became 'the retained and reclaimable byte arenas' (design.txt:322), and the x_data clause is at design.txt:333. The Words row at design.txt:28 was NOT rewritten and still names one unspecified 'additional cache storage region'. - (3) is only implied: design.txt:332 says restore must not restart retained objects, and design.txt:333 says 'once'. The design never states that the EAGLE slot lives in the retained arena. In the code it does: storage_location returns reclaimable = false for offset.i == logical_slot_count, so the EAGLE slot is at offsets.values[logical_slot_count].retained [kv_cache.hpp:727-735], and arena_sizes adds one slot to result.retained when support_eagle [kv_cache.hpp:717-719]; restore_reclaimable_kv_storage re-allocates only the reclaimable arena [kv_cache.hpp:968]. - (2) is absent. The design nowhere says EAGLE requires uniform geometry. The code requires it: eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0 [kv_cache.hpp:771] and TRON_ASSERT(!support_eagle || eagle_compatible, "EAGLE cache views require uniform geometry and embedding storage") [kv_cache.hpp:788-789]. Under the design's own rule (uniform geometry = one array over the whole arena, design.txt:331), the EAGLE slot is already covered, because the retained arena byte count includes it [kv_cache.hpp:717-719, :1161-1165]. Net: the buffer ambiguity is removed and the x_data rule is stated; the uniform-geometry precondition, the retained-arena location and the Words row are still missing. Grade: partly.

Still needed: Three edits. (a) Add to the design.txt:333 bullet: "EAGLE requires uniform geometry (kv_cache.hpp:771, 788-789). Its KV slot is the last primary-geometry slot of the RETAINED arena (storage_location returns reclaimable = false for it, kv_cache.hpp:727-735; arena_sizes adds it to retained, :717-719). The uniform one-array construction of the retained arena therefore covers it; the heterogeneous enumeration never meets an EAGLE slot. Restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena (:968), so the EAGLE slot is constructed once, in the constructor." (b) Rewrite the Words row at design.txt:28: "EAGLE is the speculative model. With EAGLE on, a book holds (a) one extra KV storage slot with the primary geometry at the end of the retained arena and (b) an embedding buffer x_data (x_bytes per token) that holds no kv_block." (c) Move or qualify the sentence "Construction cannot rely solely on the logical active-slot loop" so it does not read as an instruction for the heterogeneous path (see new defect).

source re-grader (Partly): Round-1 C01 asked for four things (r1-findings.md lines 106-113): name the two EAGLE extras separately, say that EAGLE requires uniform geometry so the per-arena one-array construction already covers the extra KV slot, say that restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena so the EAGLE slot is constructed once, and fix the Words row plus the 'both byte arenas' sentence. I re-read the revised design and the source. Met: design.txt:333 names the physical EAGLE KV slot with the primary geometry and says x_data holds no KV blocks; design.txt:322 now says 'the retained and reclaimable byte arenas'. Both statements match the code: x_data is a separate DMA buffer (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1106-1113, :1131; comment :810-812 'Retained KV, reclaimable KV, and EAGLE embeddings are separate buffers'), the EAGLE slot is offset logical_slot_count() with the primary geometry (:906-909, :1326-1329), and for_each_active_slot visits only slot < logical_slot_count() (:1243-1248), so 'the logical active-slot loop omits that extra physical slot' is right. Not met: (1) the design never says EAGLE requires uniform geometry; the code requires it at compile time (:771 'eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0'), in an assert (:788-789 'EAGLE cache views require uniform geometry and embedding storage') and in the allocation-size check (:1158-1159 returns nullopt when support_eagle && !eagle_compatible). grep of design.txt for 'uniform' finds only lines 87 and 331, neither about EAGLE. (2) The design never says the EAGLE slot lives in the retained arena; storage_location returns reclaimable = false for offset.i == logical_slot_count (:731-734) and arena_sizes adds one slot to result.retained when support_eagle (:717-719), so under design.txt:331 the retained arena's one array already covers it, and design.txt:333 'once' leaves an implementer unsure whether a second construction is needed. (3) restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena (:968) and the design says this only indirectly (design.txt:332 'must not restart objects in the retained arena'). (4) The Words row at design.txt:28 is byte-for-byte the round-1 text ('EAGLE is the speculative model with an additional cache storage region'). The checker's new defect (EAGLE bullet placed after the heterogeneous bullet reads as a heterogeneous-path instruction) is a fair 'note': EAGLE and heterogeneous geometry never coexist (:771, :788-789, :1158-1159), so the worst outcome is unreachable code, not a wrong build. Correction: The checker's assessment is right. One addition to residual (a): cite kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1158-1159 as well (calculate_allocation_sizes returns std::nullopt when support_eagle && !eagle_compatible), since that is the runtime guard that makes 'the heterogeneous enumeration never meets an EAGLE slot' true even when asserts are compiled out.

fairness re-grader (Partly): Round 1 asked for four things (r1-findings.md:106-113, verifier narrowing): (a) name the EAGLE KV slot (EAGLE = the speculative draft model that shares the cache) as one primary-geometry slot at the END of the RETAINED arena, covered by the per-arena one-array construction because EAGLE requires uniform geometry; (b) say restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena, so the EAGLE slot is constructed once, in the constructor; (c) add a clause that x_data (the separate embedding buffer) holds no kv_block and is untouched; (d) rewrite the Words row. Met: (a) in part and (c). design.txt:333 reads "Include the physical EAGLE KV slot once, with the primary geometry. Do not touch x_data, the separate EAGLE embedding buffer; it contains no KV blocks." That matches the code: eagle_storage_offset() = kv_storage_offset(logical_slot_count()) [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:906-909]; kv_block_at_storage asserts geometry == layout_t::primary_geometry for it [:1326-1329]; x_data is a separate DMA buffer [:1131, :1106-1113, :810-812]. design.txt:322 now says "the retained and reclaimable byte arenas". The code requires it three times: eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0 [:771]; TRON_ASSERT "EAGLE cache views require uniform geometry and embedding storage" [:788-789]; calculate_allocation_sizes returns nullopt when support_eagle && (!eagle_compatible || logical_slot_count == 0) [:1158-1159]. The retained-arena location is absent: "retained arena" appears only at design.txt:332 ("must not restart objects in the retained arena"). The code puts the EAGLE slot there: storage_location returns reclaimable = false for offset.i == logical_slot_count [:731-734] and arena_sizes adds offsets.values[1].total() to result.retained when support_eagle [:717-719]. (b) is only implied: restore calls allocate_kv_group(/*reclaimable=*/true, ...) only [:968], and the design says "once" at :333, but never connects the two. (d) not done: design.txt:28 is byte-identical to the round-1 "Original design said" text in r1-findings.md:110 ("EAGLE is the speculative model with an additional cache storage region"). (1) Raise the new defect from note to minor: the checker's own residual (c) asks to change the sentence, and "minor = should change". The sentence at design.txt:333 ("Construction cannot rely solely on the logical active-slot loop, which omits that extra physical slot") follows the heterogeneous bullet (:332), and the uniform bullet (:331) uses no loop at all, so the only loop it can refer to is the heterogeneous enumeration. An agent would add an EAGLE branch there. That branch is unreachable at construction time, not only asserted: calculate_allocation_sizes refuses the combination before any arena exists [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1158-1159], in addition to the assert at :788-789. Under the design's own uniform rule (:331, bound = arena byte count / sizeof(kv_block_t)) the EAGLE slot is already constructed, because its bytes are inside retained_kv_bytes_ [:717-719, :1161-1165]. (2) Add :1158-1159 to the residual's evidence list. The rest of the checker's assessment and the three residual edits are right.

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked section 6 to name the two scheduler rules that encode the V pair layout outside the cache: adjust_grains_for_partners (the minibatch splitter in model.hpp that keeps the even and odd token of a pair in one minibatch) and token_ix_needed (the page-readiness check in common.hpp). The function decides whether a minibatch depends on token tok by scanning every visible range of the page that contains tok [common.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1028-1035]. It has no even/odd or partner logic. It is a page-readiness rule; the pair rule is adjust_grains_for_partners. (c) Ambiguity: "Update their explanatory comments" applies to both functions but says what neither comment should say. The token_ix_needed comment stays true after the parent (scaled_v still reads whole pages, design.txt:316), so nothing needs to change there; the round-1 verifier said both comments stay unchanged. The model.hpp:211 comment names page.set_v, and the revised design keeps page::set_v by name and makes it forward to append_v_row (design.txt:252), so that comment also stays literally true; an update is optional and the design gives no replacement text. Line numbers are not given, but the design tells the implementer to relocate citations on fetched main (design.txt:120), and function names are stable, so that is acceptable.

Partly C07. Child layout test calls kernel functions on raw arrays; 'retain' needs a decision (round-1 grade Minor)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: checker: Partly, source: Partly, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design.txt:385 "Adapt t_k_vnni_layout to create actual aligned k_vnni_tensor owners and call typed store/load/block/reader operations through as_view(). Retain the independent index expectations. For physical-byte checks, copy the trivially copyable owner's object representation into a test buffer. Do not use detail::vnni_access to recreate raw production calls." design.txt:369 "Define k_vnni_tensor, k_vnni_view, and its row expression in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp. This header contains the K mapping and storage operations without including attention kernels. Let h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp include it for the software score reader, avoiding a tensor/kernel include cycle." design.txt:368 "Port the K mapping and vector routines from h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp, existing t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp cases, ..." design.txt:401 "Retain layout, shared-save, and AMX numerical cases. Use typed owners." design.txt:328 "Require trivial default construction, copyability, and destruction for both owner and block." design.txt:469 (section 9) "... C05 C07 | Accepted as future child work | ... typed-owner tests ..."

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked the design to state the form of the adapted child layout test: build k_vnni_tensor owners, call the typed row store, row load, block store and software reader through as_view(), keep the index anchor cases, and not use detail::vnni_access. The verifiers added three precision points: do not force stack allocation, say how a test obtains an owner's bytes for the memcmp checks, and say whether k_vnni::index stays a public constexpr function or becomes a static member of k_vnni_view (the STATIC_REQUIRE anchors call it by name). Line 385 meets the main ask and two of the three precision points. It names the owner type, the four typed operations, the as_view() entry point and the detail::vnni_access ban. It does not say "on the stack", so the test's current heap allocation via std::make_unique<plane_and_rows> [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:99, 173-174, 262] may continue. It answers the bytes question with "copy the trivially copyable owner's object representation into a test buffer", which is valid because the K owner lives inside kv_block, whose trivial copyability line 328 requires; this replaces the raw plane reads and memcmp calls at [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:120-122, 143, 202, 229]. The design's list of typed operations matches the three raw-pointer cases: scatter_row [:113], gather_row [:129], store_block [:201], qk_group [:306-308]. The gap: "Retain the independent index expectations" keeps the expected positions of the anchor case [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:74-91, using tron::k_vnni::index; at :80] but does not say what those anchors call once line 369 moves the K mapping into h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp. An implementing agent must guess between a public constexpr free function (k_vnni::index, in the new header) and a static mapping member of k_vnni_view. Both are valid; the design should pick one so the anchors can be written without a decision.

Still needed: Add one clause to design.txt:385, for example: "The index anchors call the public constexpr k_vnni::index(token, dim) that moves with the mapping into h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp" (or, if the mapping becomes a view member: "call k_vnni_view's static mapping function"). Pick one spelling.

source re-grader (Partly): design.txt:385 meets the main ask of round 1: it names the owner type (k_vnni_tensor), the typed operations ("store/load/block/reader"), the entry point (as_view()) and the ban on detail::vnni_access (the internal raw-storage friend, design.txt:223). It also meets two of the three precision points the round-1 verifiers added: it says "aligned" rather than "on the stack", so the test's heap allocation via std::make_unique<plane_and_rows> may continue [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:99, 173-174, 262]; and it says how a test reads an owner's bytes ("copy the trivially copyable owner's object representation into a test buffer"), which replaces the raw plane reads and memcmp calls [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:120-122, 143, 202, 229]. The list of typed operations matches the three raw-pointer cases: scatter_row [:113, :139-140, :199, :214, :226], gather_row [:129, :232], store_block [:201, :228], qk_group [:306-309]. Two gaps remain. (1) Kind (c) ambiguity: "Retain the independent index expectations" keeps the anchor case but does not say what those anchors call. Today they call the public constexpr free function tron::k_vnni::index(token, dim) [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:101-107] through using tron::k_vnni::index; and STATIC_REQUIRE [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:80-90]. design.txt:369 moves "the K mapping" into h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp and design.txt:57 says "Put the address formula inside each concrete view", so the implementer must choose between a retained public free function and a static member of k_vnni_view; the round-1 verifier named this as something the design must state, and the revision does not. (2) Kind (c) ambiguity the checker did not list: the existing cases also WRITE raw bytes into the plane, not only read them. They fill the plane with poison [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:107-109, 190-192] and copy one plane onto another with memcpy [:193, :216]. design.txt:385 covers only the read direction ("copy ... into a test buffer"). With no public pointer constructor or .data on packed views (design.txt:222) and the vnni_access ban, the test needs a stated way to fill an owner with arbitrary bytes. Trivial copyability (design.txt:385 "trivially copyable owner"; design.txt:328 for the block) permits memcpy into the owner or std::bit_cast from a poisoned array, and defaulted owner copy (design.txt:210 for the V owner) replaces the plane-to-plane memcpy, but the design should say so instead of leaving the agent to infer it. Correction: Keep the checker's residual and add one sentence to it: "Prefill and poison writes into a k_vnni_tensor owner use memcpy into the trivially copyable owner or std::bit_cast from a poisoned array of the same size; plane-to-plane copies use the owner's defaulted copy assignment." The checker's residual on the index anchors is right as written; pick one spelling (retained public constexpr k_vnni::index in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp, or a static mapping member of k_vnni_view).

Correction: Checker residual (2) says the aligned flag 'states that the plane base is 64-byte aligned'. That number holds only in the 16-lane build. The flag's actual meaning: aligned = true makes row chunk reads and writes use the aligned vector load and store forms through chunky<T, true> (tron_mm_load_bf16 / tron_mm_store_bf16) instead of the unaligned chunky<T, false> forms [h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:29-59@2880c3aa9b; h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:157-158 and 189-191@2880c3aa9b]. The required alignment is chunk_alignment = chunk_size * sizeof(float) [h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:87@2880c3aa9b]: 64 bytes in the 16-lane build, 32 bytes in the 8-lane build. Suggested sentence for design.txt:203-205: 'The second template argument, aligned = true, promises chunk_alignment (64 bytes at 16 lanes, 32 bytes at 8 lanes) so chunk reads use aligned vector loads; it matches the existing kv_block::k_view() type [kv_cache.hpp:2210@f46e48bab498].' Also add to residual (1) that design.txt:180 is new revision text, so the revision introduced this first-use gap rather than leaving the round-1 one in place.

That item is absent from the round-1 F23 claim and recommendation as codex received them [prior-review.txt:867-897]; it appears only inside one verifier correction in r1-findings.md ("narrow the view-flag item to the aligned flag only"). Partly F35. Row chunk/set mechanics and override signature unspecified (round-1 grade Minor)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: checker: Partly, source: Partly, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design.txt:220 "row.chunk(i) | Return fp32 values in logical order. Read pair chunk i at pair_base + 2 * chunk_size * i. Extract the even or odd half with vector instructions." design.txt:221 "bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t i) const noexcept | Use this exact non-template override signature. Extract stored bf16 bits directly. The expression base detects the override through its member function; a different signature can silently select conversion instead." design.txt:225 "For the 16-lane build, a pair chunk loads 32 bf16 elements in 64 bytes. The existing even_part shifts each 32-bit lane left by 16 bits; odd_part masks the high 16 bits. Reuse this extraction pattern for fp32 reads and narrow the selected halves for bf16 reads. A stride-2 ordinary row view has the right addresses but uses scalar extraction; it is not the bulk-read implementation. [S5] [F35]" design.txt:229 "There is no generic packed row.set(expr) in the parent." design.txt:241 "append_v_row moves today's set_v vector bodies into h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp." design.txt:398 (Expression reads row, failure column) "The new type cannot be consumed by expr, or silently takes a lossy fallback." design.txt:440 "Inspect the caller bodies containing bf16/fp16/float even and odd V appends, packed token copies, weighted V sums, and arena allocation/restore."

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked for (a) the chunk-to-pair mechanics, (b) the exact bf16_chunk override signature and how the expr base detects it, (c) the set/merge mechanics, (d) a sentence rejecting the stride-2 view, and, per the verifier corrections, (e) a note that a missed override is bit-exact but slower plus adding the bf16 read path to the generated-instruction comparison. The revision meets (a), (b), (c) and (d). Checked: the address rule "pair_base + 2 * chunk_size * i" in bf16 elements matches the existing get_v loops, which load _mm512_load_si512(v_ptr + i * 2) while i steps 16 dimensions (kv_cache.hpp:2416-2418@f46e48bab498); even rows use _mm512_slli_epi32(both, 16) (:2420) and odd rows _mm512_and_si512(both, 0xffff0000) (:2424-2429); the bf16 reads narrow with _mm512_cvtepi32_epi16 (:2454, :2462), so "narrow the selected halves for bf16 reads" is right. The override signature matches the base exactly: expr.hpp:110-117@f46e48bab498 declares bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t i) const noexcept and tests if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk); existing overrides use the same form (h/tron/hardware/permuted.hpp:53, h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:367@f46e48bab498). The stride-2 rejection is right: the rank-1 view's chunk() gathers scalars and set() stores scalars when s0 != 1 (h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:155-166, 186-204@f46e48bab498). The set/merge mechanics are covered by moving the set_v bodies and by deferring generic row.set (design.txt:229, 241, 277). Two slips remain. First, design.txt:221 "a different signature can silently select conversion instead" is factually wrong: only omitting the member is silent (then &B::bf16_chunk names the inherited base member and compares equal); a different parameter type, return type, const-qualification, an overload set, or a template makes the != in the if-constexpr condition ill-formed, which is a hard compile error at expr.hpp:112, and a missing noexcept still compares unequal so the override is used. The round-1 verifier corrections said exactly this. Second, design.txt:398 calls the fallback "lossy"; fp32s_to_bf16s(chunk(i)) (h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:92-109@f46e48bab498) is bit-exact for values that came from bf16 because chunk() widens by a 16-bit shift, the low 16 bits are zero, the NaN mask never fires, and srli 16 plus cvtepi32_epi16 returns the original bits; the cost is an extra convert, not a loss. Because the fallback is bit-exact, the bit-pattern checks at design.txt:396 and 398 cannot detect a missing override, and the objdump inspection list at design.txt:440 omits the bf16 read path, so item (e) is not met.

Still needed: 1) Replace the last sentence of design.txt:221 with: "Omitting bf16_chunk silently selects the base's fp32s_to_bf16s(chunk(i)) path; a mismatched signature fails to compile at the base's member-pointer comparison [expr.hpp:112@f46e48bab498]." 2) In design.txt:398 replace "silently takes a lossy fallback" with "silently takes the fp32 round-trip fallback, which is bit-exact for stored bf16 but slower", and add "exact bf16 row reads (bf16_chunk)" to the inspected regions at design.txt:440 so the objdump comparison detects a missing override.

source re-grader (Partly): Round 1 asked for (a) chunk-to-pair mechanics, (b) the exact bf16_chunk override signature and how the expr base (expr<B, N>, the rank-1 expression base class) detects it, (c) set/merge mechanics, (d) a sentence rejecting the stride-2 view, and, per the verifier corrections, (e) a statement that a missed override is bit-exact but slower plus adding the bf16 read path to the generated-instruction comparison. Items (a)-(d) are met and I re-derived them. (a) "Read pair chunk i at pair_base + 2 * chunk_size * i" [design.txt:220] matches the existing get_v loops, which load _mm512_load_si512(v_ptr + i * 2) with v_ptr a bf16 pointer and i stepping 16 dimensions [kv_cache.hpp:2413-2418@f46e48bab498], i.e. 32 bf16 elements per 16-dimension chunk. Even rows use _mm512_slli_epi32(both, 16) [:2420], odd rows _mm512_and_si512(both, hi_16_of_32) [:2429], and the bf16 destinations narrow with _mm512_cvtepi32_epi16 [:2454, :2462], matching design.txt:225. (b) bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t i) const noexcept [design.txt:221] is exactly the base's form [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:111@f46e48bab498] and the existing overrides' form [h/tron/hardware/permuted.hpp:53, h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:367@f46e48bab498]; detection is if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk) [expr.hpp:112]. (c) is covered by moving the set_v bodies into append_v_row and deferring generic row.set [design.txt:229, 241, 277]. (d) [design.txt:225] is right: the rank-1 view's chunk() gathers scalars and set() stores scalars when s0 != 1 [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:155-166, 186-204@f46e48bab498]. Item (e) is not met and the revision adds two factual slips. Slip 1: "a different signature can silently select conversion instead" [design.txt:221]. Only omitting the member is silent, because &B::bf16_chunk then names the inherited base member and the comparison is equal. A different parameter type, return type or const-qualification gives two pointer-to-member types with no common type, so the != at expr.hpp:112 is a hard compile error whenever the base function is instantiated, and it is instantiated by every bf16 hardware-tensor consumer, which calls rhs.bf16_chunk(i) through expr<B, N> const& [dmatensor.hpp:272-276, 293-296@f46e48bab498]. A missing noexcept converts and compares unequal, so the override is used. Slip 2: "silently takes a lossy fallback" [design.txt:398]. The fallback fp32s_to_bf16s(chunk(i)) ORs 0x00010000 only where the exponent field is saturated AND the low 16 bits are nonzero, then shifts right 16 and narrows [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:96-109 (AVX-512) and :60-87 (AVX2)@f46e48bab498]. A packed row's chunk() leaves the low 16 bits zero (shift left 16, or mask 0xffff0000), so the correction never fires and the round trip returns the stored bits. The fallback is bit-exact and only slower, so the bit-pattern checks at design.txt:396 and :398 cannot detect a missing override. The objdump inspection list at design.txt:440 names appends, token copies, weighted sums and arena allocation/restore but not the bf16 read path, so the omission stays undetectable. I agree with partly. Correction: The checker's residual is right and needs one addition that makes the gap larger than stated. The test row at design.txt:398 says "Construct an ordinary host tensor from the packed matrix view. Check row chunks and exact bf16 copies" and only optionally "Use an existing hardware tensor fixture if it already supports this input." An ordinary host tensor never calls bf16_chunk: tensor<N> constructs and assigns from an expression with store_chunk(i, rhs.chunk(i)), the fp32 path [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:81-85, 125-129@f46e48bab498], and a git grep for bf16_chunk over h and src at f46e48bab498 finds callers only in dmatensor.hpp (:276, :296, :316, :329), permuted.hpp (:53, its own override) and expr.hpp (:715-716, a forwarding wrapper). So the design's proposed check, as written, does not exercise the override at all, and even a dmatensor<bf16> consumer would pass with the fallback because it is bit-exact. Add to the residual: (3) In design.txt:398 replace the optional hardware-tensor sentence with a required one: "Call row.bf16_chunk(i) directly, or assign the row to a bf16 dmatensor [dmatensor.hpp:272-276], because host tensors read rows through chunk() only [tensor.hpp:83, 127]; a bit check passes with or without the override, so the objdump comparison at design.txt:440 is the only detector." The two rewordings the checker gives for design.txt:221 and :398 stand as written. Severity of the whole stays minor: the actionable guidance (use the exact signature) is already correct, so the risk is an undetected extra convert on the bf16 read path, not wrong values.

Partly F41. NaN divergence between set_v truncation and generic conversion unstated (round-1 grade Minor)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: checker: Partly, source: Partly, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design.txt:318: "Packed set_v can turn an fp32 NaN with no upper mantissa bits into infinity when it discards the lower bits. Generic fp32s_to_bf16s, the expression conversion helper, sets the lowest retained mantissa bit when the exponent is all ones and discarded bits are nonzero. It skips that correction when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined. This preserves a NaN but does not necessarily make it a quiet NaN. Neither path rounds to nearest. Preserve each existing path separately. [S5] [S7]". design.txt:313-314: "Packed V append from bf16 | Preserve exact input bits. No float round trip." / "Packed V append from fp16 / float | Keep today's conversion to fp32 and upper-16-bit truncation. Do not substitute general expression conversion." design.txt:396 (test row): "Use independently specified expected bit patterns around truncation boundaries, infinity, and NaN. Verify bf16 bulk load/copy exactly. Keep packed append and generic expression conversion expectations separate." design.txt:474: "F41 | Accepted; example corrected | Preserve packed/generic conversion differences. Limit the NaN-to-infinity example to fp32 input; the review's fp16 example omitted instruction-level NaN handling."

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked for three things: state the exact NaN divergence rule, give the worked example (fp32 0x7F800001 becomes 0x7F80 = +Inf under the packed set_v truncation, 0x7F81 under fp32s_to_bf16s), and tell the test author that expected bits differ per path and per build type (TRON_IGNORE_NAN). The round-1 verifiers withdrew the fp16 example (the hardware fp16-to-fp32 conversion quiets the NaN first), and the design's section 9 row records that correctly. The revised rule text at design.txt:318 is factually right on every checkable point. fp32s_to_bf16s (the generic fp32-to-bf16 conversion) ORs 0x00010000 into any lane whose exponent field is 0x7f800000 and whose low 16 bits are nonzero, then shifts right by 16 [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:62-71 (AVX2) and 92-109 (AVX-512) @f46e48bab498; the file is unchanged at 2880c3aa9b]. Bit 16 becomes bf16 bit 0, the lowest mantissa bit, not the quiet bit, so "does not necessarily make it a quiet NaN" is right. Both bodies are wrapped in #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN and skip the correction when it is defined [bf16.hpp:57-58 and 93-95 @f46e48bab498]. Two parts of the recommendation are still missing. (1) No worked example: the text says "an fp32 NaN with no upper mantissa bits" but never gives 0x7F800001 -> 0x7F80 versus 0x7F81, and "no upper mantissa bits" is loose (it means fp32 mantissa bits 22 to 16 all zero). (2) The build-type consequence is absent: TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined for every non-Debug configuration [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:267-270 @f46e48bab498; 292-295 and 314-317 @2880c3aa9b: "$<$<AND:${CXX_GccOrClang},$<NOT:$<CONFIG:Debug>>>:-O3;-DTRON_IGNORE_NAN;-DTRON_IGNORE_FTZ>"], and the required Nix test build is RelWithDebInfo [nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:80 @2880c3aa9b]. So in CI and production both paths truncate identically, and a hard-coded NaN expectation for the generic (8-lane row-view .set()) path passes in one build type and fails in the other. The test row at design.txt:396 says only "Keep packed append and generic expression conversion expectations separate", which does not warn the implementing agent about the build-type dependence. This is the part with a practical consequence, so the finding is partly addressed.

Still needed: At design.txt:318 replace "an fp32 NaN with no upper mantissa bits" with "an fp32 NaN whose upper 7 mantissa bits (bits 22-16) are zero, for example 0x7F800001, which set_v stores as 0x7F80 (+Inf) and fp32s_to_bf16s stores as 0x7F81 when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is not defined". Add one sentence: "TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined for every non-Debug build (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt, the tron target_compile_options generator expression), including the RelWithDebInfo Nix test build, so outside Debug both paths truncate identically." In the test row at design.txt:396 add: "NaN expected bits for the generic conversion path depend on CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE (TRON_IGNORE_NAN); either test both cases under #ifdef or restrict NaN cases to the packed append path, which always truncates."

Bit 16 becomes bf16 bit 0, the lowest mantissa bit, not the quiet bit (bf16 bit 6), so "does not necessarily make it a quiet NaN" is right. The correction is skipped under #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN [bf16.hpp:57-58, 93-95]. Two parts of the round-1 recommendation remain missing. Existing precedent the design could point to: t/t_bf16.cpp:97-99 @2880c3aa9b already warns "this test may fail on some hardware if IGNORE_NAN is set" and uses only quiet NaNs (inf-inf, 0/0), which survive truncation on both paths. First, say that TRON_IGNORE_NAN is a PUBLIC compile option of the tron target [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:292-295 @2880c3aa9b], so test executables that link tron compile with it too; otherwise a reader may think only library code is affected. Second, in the test-row addition, name the existing precedent: t/t_bf16.cpp:97-99 @2880c3aa9b ("bf16 preserves nan") avoids the build-type dependence by using quiet NaNs only (inf-inf and 0/0, bit 22 set), so the design can say: use quiet NaNs for expectations shared by both paths, and put the signalling-NaN case (0x7F800001) only on the packed append path, which always truncates.

fairness re-grader (Partly): Round 1 asked for three things: the exact NaN divergence rule, a worked example, and per-path expected bits for the test author; the verifiers added that the divergence exists only when TRON_IGNORE_NAN (a compile-time define) is not set, and that the test row must say so [r1-findings.md F41 Recommendation and Verifier corrections 2-4]. The rule is now stated and is correct: design.txt:318 says packed set_v (the cache's V write) can turn an fp32 NaN with no upper mantissa bits into infinity, that fp32s_to_bf16s (the generic fp32-to-bf16 conversion) sets the lowest retained mantissa bit when the exponent is all ones and the discarded bits are nonzero, and that it skips this when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined. I confirmed each clause against h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:57-71 (AVX2) and 93-108 (AVX-512) at 2880c3aa9b, where the OR of 0x00010000 is inside #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN / #else and the shift right by 16 follows; the file is unchanged from f46e48bab498 (git diff --stat empty). The per-path guidance is met in substance by the table rows at design.txt:312-314 (row-major V keeps row-view .set() conversion; packed V from fp16/float keeps fp32 conversion plus upper-16-bit truncation), and view::set does call chunky<bf16,true>::set, which calls fp32s_to_bf16s [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:191 and h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:55-57 @2880c3aa9b]. Two concrete parts are missing. First, no worked example: neither 0x7F800001 nor 0x7F80/0x7F81 appears anywhere in design.txt (grep for 0x7F returns nothing), although the section 9 row says "example corrected" [design.txt:474]. Second, the build-type consequence is absent: TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined for every non-Debug configuration [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:293 and 316 @2880c3aa9b; :268 @f46e48bab498], and the Nix test build is RelWithDebInfo [nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:80 @2880c3aa9b], so in CI and production both paths truncate identically and a hard-coded NaN expectation for the generic path passes in Debug only. The test row at design.txt:396 says only "Keep packed append and generic expression conversion expectations separate" and does not warn about this. design.txt contains no occurrence of Debug, RelWithDebInfo or CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE. Correction: The checker's residual is right. Add one item: the section 9 row for F41 [design.txt:474] says "Accepted; example corrected", but the design text contains no worked example at all, so either insert the fp32 example the checker proposes at design.txt:318 or change the row to say the example was removed. Also state the direction plainly for the test author: with TRON_IGNORE_NAN defined (all non-Debug builds, including the required Nix RelWithDebInfo build) fp32s_to_bf16s gives 0x7F80 for input 0x7F800001, the same as set_v; only a Debug build gives 0x7F81.

Partly F54. K is transposed V formula per tile, not per plane (round-1 grade Note)

Checker status: Partly. Re-graders: checker: Partly, source: Partly, fairness: Partly.

Design text checked: design.txt:177 table row: "Blocked packed K | ((((dimension / 32) * (R / 16) + token / 16) * 16 + (dimension % 32) / 2) * 16 + token % 16) * 2 + dimension % 2 | PR #4424 only. Keep the existing layout-selection condition. Keep the kernel restricted to 64 tokens × 128 dimensions." design.txt:178: "R is the stored token count. D is the stored dimension count. The packed-K formula uses groups of 32 dimensions and groups of 16 tokens. Within a tile, K uses the transposed packing idea. Across the plane, its 16-token and 32-dimension block order is also required; swapping the two plane coordinates alone is insufficient. [S1] [S10]" design.txt:476 (section 9 row): "F54 F57 F58 F59 | Recorded; no new implementation scope | Clarify per-tile versus whole-plane K mapping. ..."

Checker assessment: Round 1 (a note) asked for one appended sentence: within each 16-token x 32-dimension tile the blocked-K offset equals the packed-V formula applied with row = dimension % 32 and column = token % 16, tiles ordered dimension-step major then token-block minor, said to apply to the child PR only, and without the claim that pair helpers can be shared. The revision added the sentence "Within a tile, K uses the transposed packing idea" plus "swapping the two plane coordinates alone is insufficient" (design.txt:178). The facts in the new text are right. The formula in the table row equals k_vnni::index() at h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:101-107@30c4ac82cbb6 and the header comment at :22-26 (s = 32 dimensions, c = 16 tokens, order (s*4+c), with R/16 = TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 for R = 64). My enumeration over 64 tokens x 128 dimensions: a whole-plane swap of token and dimension in the V formula mismatches 7680 of 8192 positions; the tile-level relation (base (s*4+c)*512, in-tile offset (dimension%32/2)*32 + 2*(token%16) + dimension%2) matches 8192 of 8192. The revision did not add the pair-helper claim, which is what the verifiers wanted dropped. What is missing is precision: "the transposed packing idea" is undefined shorthand (kind (c) ambiguity), it does not say transposed relative to the packed-V formula, it does not say which coordinate becomes the row inside the tile, and the tile order (dimension-step major, token-block minor) is carried only by the formula in the table, not by the prose. "PR #4424 only" appears in the table row, so the child-only scope is present. The sentence also joins two claims with a semicolon (plain-English rule 8), a style slip only. Severity of the residual: minor (the finding was a note).

Still needed: Replace "Within a tile, K uses the transposed packing idea." in section 4 (design.txt:178) with: "Within each tile of 16 tokens x 32 dimensions (dimension step s = dimension / 32, token block c = token / 16), at element base (s*4 + c)*512, the blocked-K offset equals the packed-V formula applied to a 32-row x 16-column plane with row = dimension % 32 and column = token % 16, that is (dimension % 32 / 2)*32 + 2*(token % 16) + dimension % 2. Tiles are ordered dimension-step major, token-block minor. This applies to PR #4424 only." Split the semicolon sentence into two sentences.

source re-grader (Partly): Round 1 (a note) asked for one appended sentence giving the tile-level relation between the blocked-K formula (the child PR's K layout) and the packed-V formula, with the tile size, the in-tile row/column assignment, the tile order, child-only scope, and without the pair-helper claim. The revision's text is design.txt:178: "Within a tile, K uses the transposed packing idea. Across the plane, its 16-token and 32-dimension block order is also required; swapping the two plane coordinates alone is insufficient." I re-derived the facts. The table formula at design.txt:176 equals k_vnni::index() at h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:101-107@30c4ac82cbb6 (s = dim/32, c = token/16, dp = (dim%32)/2, t = token%16, j = dim%2; TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 = R/16 at R = 64) and the header formula at :25-26. My own enumeration over 64 tokens x 128 dimensions: swapping token and dimension in the packed-V formula over the whole plane mismatches 7680 of 8192 positions; the tile relation (base (s*4+c)*512, in-tile offset (dim%32/2)*32 + 2*(token%16) + dim%2) matches 8192 of 8192, and the K map is a bijection. So every fact in the new sentence is right and the pair-helper claim was correctly left out. What is missing is precision (kind (c) ambiguity): the word "tile" occurs exactly once in the whole design (design.txt:178) and is never defined, so the 16-token x 32-dimension size is only inferable from the formula; "the transposed packing idea" does not say transposed relative to the packed-V formula nor which coordinate becomes the in-tile row; the tile order (dimension-step major, token-block minor) is carried only by the formula. "PR #4424 only" is present in the table row (design.txt:176). Severity minor; the original finding was a note. Checker's quotes and enumeration counts match mine. Correction: Checker's residual arithmetic is correct. Two refinements to it: (1) write the tile base as (s * (R / 16) + c) * 512 elements rather than (s*4 + c)*512, so the prose matches the table's R/16 form (4 = R/16 only at R = 64, the kernel's fixed page size); (2) name the unit the way the child code does: k_vnni.hpp:27-28@30c4ac82cbb6 calls one (s, c) block "one 1 KiB panel: 16 dimension-pair rows of 64 bytes. A panel is exactly one AMX B tile". Writing "tile (one 16-token x 32-dimension panel, one AMX B tile in k_vnni.hpp)" defines the term at first use and lets the implementer find it in the child source.

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked for a child accessor table covering the five page members PR 4424 adds (k_vnni_plane, set_k_row, get_k_row, set_k_block, the !layout_on requires-clauses on page::k), an explicit statement that the typed store_block keeps its input shape (16 independent row pointers, null allowed for absent lanes, never a contiguous 16-row buffer), and a statement of where k_vnni_view is declared so kernels/k_vnni.hpp (included by kv_cache.hpp) does not create an include cycle with the tensor header. The revision adds exactly that table [design.txt:374-381] and the header placement [design.txt:369]. Each row matches the child source. kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:1689 const bf16* k_vnni_plane(kv_slot_id slot, size_t kv_head) const noexcept is the raw accessor the table removes. :1701-1705 set_k_row(slot, kv_head, i_page, const bf16* row) calls k_vnni::scatter_row; :1737-1741 get_k_row calls k_vnni::gather_row; the table keeps both names and moves the address math into the K type. :1723-1730 set_k_block(kv_slot_id slot, size_t kv_head, size_t c, __mmask16 present, const bf16* const rows[k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16]) calls k_vnni::store_block(plane, c, present, rows); the design's store_block(view, block, mask, rows) maps plane->view, c->block, present->mask one to one. The null-lane rule matches k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:186-187 "rows[t] points at the 128 bf16 of token t. It may be null for an absent token." and the signature at :194-197. The page::k overloads at kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:1619-1674 all carry !k_vnni::layout_on<...>, which the table keeps. qk_group, named in the "Copy and score readers" row, is the AVX-512 reader at k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:248 (the "software score reader" of design.txt:369). The include-cycle answer is sound. kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:27 includes tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp; k_vnni.hpp includes only <immintrin.h> and common/ headers (:32-40); the tensor headers include kernels/expr.hpp and kernels/chunky.hpp (view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:6, views.hpp:6) but no kernels/k_vnni.hpp. So the proposed chain tensor/k_vnni.hpp <- kernels/k_vnni.hpp <- kv_cache.hpp has no cycle. h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp exists at neither 30c4ac82cbb6 nor 2880c3aa9b, so it is a new file as the design intends. Two headers share the basename k_vnni.hpp in different directories; tron already does this (h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp and common/numerics/bf16.hpp), and the design always writes full paths, so this is not a defect. Resolved C05. 'Same logical row behavior' for K invites a whole-line read-modify-write that races with the shared block save (round-1 grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: checker: Resolved, source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design.txt:383 "K stores differ from V stores. A K token owns separate 4-byte lanes in a shared cache line. Its row store may use a lane scatter or a lane-masked store; it must never read, merge, and rewrite a whole 64-byte line. Several workers can write different token lanes of that line during Note [Shared block save]. Keep that contract alongside Note [K VNNI storage]. [S10] [C05]" design.txt:378 "page::set_k_row, page::get_k_row | Keep names. Call typed store_row/load_row, moving scatter_row/gather_row address calculations into the K type's operations." design.txt:401 (Child only verification row) "Retain layout, shared-save, and AMX numerical cases. Use typed owners. Check disjoint worker lane writes followed by correct reads of all 16 block rows. Check masked-out rows and per-row source pointers." ... failure column: "Cross-token K races, bad mask behavior, wrong layout interpretation, or early completion." design.txt:469 (section 9) "F14 F15 F25 F29 F45 C04 C05 C07 | Accepted as future child work | Specify stacked base, topical reconstruction, accessor changes, lane-sized K stores, typed-owner tests, generator file, and scratch lifetime." The round-1 sentence "Give them the same logical row behavior" no longer appears anywhere in design.txt (grep for "same logical row" returns nothing).

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked for three things: (a) an explicit write-granularity rule for K rows (a K row write touches only its own token's 4-byte lanes and never loads or stores a whole 64-byte line), (b) the reason (the shared block save has several threads writing disjoint lanes of the same line), and (c) a child verification entry for disjoint-lane writes followed by a full read-back. The revision meets all three. Line 383 states the rule and the reason as a stand-alone contract and tells the implementer where to record it (next to Note [K VNNI storage]). Line 401 adds the verification entry. The ambiguous bridging sentence is removed. Factual claims in the new text check out against the child source. The child's row store is a 4-byte-lane scatter: scatter_row calls _mm512_i32scatter_epi32 [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:139-143]. The block store is lane-masked for a partial block (_mm512_mask_storeu_epi32) and a plain full-line store for a full block [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:206-213]; a full-line store without a prior read is not a read-modify-write, so it does not contradict line 383. Note [Shared block save] exists [h/tron/models/model.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:2732] and says "Their writers use masked stores on disjoint token lanes. So two threads may write one block without conflict." [model.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:2763-2765]. Note [K VNNI storage] exists [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:653]. The mixed case the rule protects is real: a run of one token goes through set_k_row (scatter) while other units of the same block go through set_k_block (masked store), both inside one shared window [model.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:2914-2941]. The verification row in line 401 corresponds in substance to the child's existing three-thread shared-save section, whose work units [5,8) [8] [9,16) share block 0 [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:2772-2810], which is what the round-1 verifier said would suffice.
