Resolved F13. Interface lacks packed-to-packed token copy for append_v (round-1 grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: checker: Resolved, source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design.txt:234-236 "copy_token(writable_v_view dst, size_t dst_token, readonly_v_view src, size_t src_token); copy_plane(v_owner& dst, v_owner const& src);" design.txt:243 "copy_token moves the four even/odd branches of today's append_v. An even destination zeros its partner. An odd destination preserves it. Retain the existing restrictions on overlap and fresh destination ranges." design.txt:244 "copy_plane copies identical-layout owners byte for byte. Cache range splitting and completion copying remain in cache code." design.txt:256 "page::append_v | Keep the name; call copy_token. | Use both blocks' kv_block_at_storage<geometry>(offset, kv_head).v.as_view() in the packed path. No new accessor by storage offset." design.txt:341 "Preserve whole-plane byte copies, the four source/destination token-parity combinations, page-boundary splitting, overlap restrictions, and completion-state copying." design.txt:380 (child table) "Copy and score readers | Use typed K token/plane copies and typed qk_vnni_128x4/qk_group arguments." design.txt:395 "... all four token-copy parity combinations."

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked for a named packed-to-packed per-token copy operation with the rule "even destination zeroes its partner, odd destination merges", implemented from today's four append_v branches, a sentence saying copy_storage_slot (the per-head token copy loop used by append and defragmentation) obtains both views from kv_block_at_storage<geometry>(offset, kv_head).v.as_view() with no new accessor by storage offset, and a note that the child adds the same pair for K. The revision names copy_token with that exact rule (lines 234-235, 243), states the kv_block_at_storage route and the no-new-accessor rule (line 256), and gives the child a typed K token/plane copy row (line 380). The factual claims are right at the design's snapshot. page::append_v has four branches: even source to even destination stores zero_b (partner zeroed), even to odd merges with a ternarylogic, odd to even stores zero_a, odd to odd merges [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1885-1919]. It reads the source block through src_page->template kv_block_at_storage<geometry>(storage_offset, kv_head).v[src_i_page / 2] and the destination through kv_block_at_storage<geometry>(storage_offset, kv_head).v[dst_i_page / 2] [kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1879-1883]. The fresh-destination restriction is the existing comment "append_v is only called via copy_from in append(), where destinations are always fresh ranges" [kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1867-1870]. copy_storage_slot calls append_v once per token in the 16-lane build [kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1943-1946]. The finding is met on substance. The added copy_plane operation, which the round-1 lead recommended and two verifiers called redundant, is reported below as a note.

I re-derived the source facts. append_v has four branches at h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1885-1919: even->even stores zero_b (:1888-1892), even->odd merges with _mm512_ternarylogic_epi32 (:1894-1901), odd->even stores zero_a (:1904-1909), odd->odd merges (:1910-1918). The child adds a whole-page memcpy for K only (if (src_begin == 0 && dst_begin == 0 && count == page_size) memcpy(dst_block.k, src_block.k, sizeof(dst_block.k)) [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:2101-2112]) and leaves the V loop unchanged. No overlap restriction exists in the source: grep -i overlap on h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498 finds nothing, and the only restriction stated for append_v is the comment "Even-destination paths zero the odd partner instead of preserving it. This is safe because append_v is only called via copy_from in append(), where destinations are always fresh ranges (dst_begin = tok_ct)" (:1867-1870). An implementer told to retain an overlap rule would search for one and have to guess. Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: checker: Resolved, source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design.txt:437 "Instruction comparison and performance acceptance"; :439 "Record the parent's actual main baseline commit and head. Build both with the same pinned compiler, preset, optimization flags, and feature options. Start with the 16-lane AMX-enabled configuration above." (the configuration table at :412 reads "cmake --preset native -DAVX512=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON"); :440 "Run objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn -C on both built t_llama_unit binaries. Inspect the caller bodies containing bf16/fp16/float even and odd V appends, packed token copies, weighted V sums, and arena allocation/restore. These helpers are often forced inline; absence of a standalone helper symbol is not a passed comparison."; :441 "Check vector extraction/merge instructions and vdpbf16ps, the vector bf16 dot product. Check for new calls, memset, repeated scalar stores, scalar dimension loops, extra even-write destination reads, and arena clears."; :442 "Define a material change as any new call, loss of the vector path, added destination read on the even path, memory-clearing operation, or changed arithmetic/reduction order. Investigate any increase in instructions or loads/stores. Instruction counts are a review signal, not a measurement of runtime."; :443 "If an unexplained hot-path change remains, compare repeated controlled timings against the same baseline on the authorized host."; :445 "Insufficient data: there is no parent implementation or runtime measurement here. No speedup or regression threshold is claimed."; :407 "Use separate build directories at the recorded baseline and parent head."; section 9 row :471 "F17 F48 F49 | Accepted; measurement limits retained | Define call-site disassembly checks ... Do not equate instruction counts with runtime."

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked for a written procedure: a named baseline, the build flags, a disassembly tool, the code to inspect, and a definition of a material change. The verifier corrections narrowed this: name the tool, say that the targeted functions are always-inline so the comparison unit is the inlined call site, map the configurations to CMake flags, gather the criteria in one place, and adopt neither a numeric threshold nor a default timing campaign. The revision does each of these. The baseline is the parent's main baseline commit built with the same preset and flags (design.txt:439). The tool is objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn -C on the t_llama_unit binary (design.txt:440); those are valid GNU binutils flags. The configuration is named by reference to the table (16-lane, AMX on = cmake --preset native -DAVX512=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON, design.txt:412); the CMake option names are right (CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:44 option(AVX512 ...), :48 option(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH ...)) and the native preset builds RelWithDebInfo (CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:31-34). The always-inline warning is correct: page::set_v is declared TRON(inline) (kv_cache.hpp@f46e48ba:1621 and the definition at :2288), append_v is TRON(inline) (:1872), scaled_v_expr::accumulate_16_chunks is TRON(inline) (:2010), and TRON(inline) expands to tron_inline = inline __attribute__((always_inline)) (h/common/attributes.hpp@2880c3aa9b:24,78). The instruction named for the weighted V sum is right: scaled_v_expr uses _mm512_dpbf16_ps, whose mnemonic is vdpbf16ps (kv_cache.hpp@f46e48ba:2019-2034, 2087-2090). t_llama_unit is a valid object to inspect: it includes model.hpp and kv_cache.hpp and instantiates scaled_v and set_v (t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:65-66, 1665-1723). The material-change criteria are consolidated in one sentence (design.txt:442), timing is conditional rather than default (design.txt:443), and no numeric threshold is claimed (design.txt:445), as the verifiers asked. The design's [F17] and [C..] bracket citations link to the round-1 page, and the section 9 row records the disposition. The finding is met on substance.

Still needed: Optional, low risk: in step 2 (design.txt:440) name the demangled caller symbols to search for in the objdump output, since the helpers have no standalone symbols: save_v_impl<...> (the page::set_v inline site), the page append/copy path that calls append_v (copy_storage_slot / copy_from), and the CPU attention caller of page::scaled_v. The design's own accessor table already names these chains (design.txt:252, 256, 257), so this is a cross-reference, not new content. Also say that "separate build directories" (design.txt:407) means separate source checkouts, because the native preset fixes binaryDir to ${sourceDir}/gen (CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:34).

The revision takes that branch explicitly: the owner does not inherit expr (210), its only read interface is as_view() with & and const & qualifiers (210), the rvalue forms including const && are deleted (210, matching the rejected-candidate F36 clarification at 479), the "insufficient" sentence is gone, and every owner use in the text goes through as_view() (256, 385) with ordinary tensors constructed from the view's expressions, not from the owner (277). The C++ overload set (&, const &, && = delete, const && = delete) is legal because all four are ref-qualified. This matches tron's rank-2 precedent, where struct tensor<d0, d1, ds...> has no expr base [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:236 @2880c3aa9b] while only rank-1 tensor<N> : expr<tensor<N>, N> does [tensor.hpp:31]. One nuance for the implementing agent, not a defect: deleting as_view() const && does not block the slice Owner& overload [h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp:38-42 @f46e48bab498] for a const prvalue owner, because inside that overload owner is an lvalue and as_view() const & is selected; that latent path is the same generic-expr-slice path recorded under F08 and needs no separate edit while packed slices have no caller.

Resolved F37. No-read pair store conflicts with odd-boundary writable slices (round-1 grade Minor)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: checker: Resolved, source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design.txt:229 "append_v_row is this design's name for the sketch's V store_row. ... an even destination zeros its odd partner; an odd destination preserves its even partner. There is no generic packed row.set(expr) in the parent." design.txt:241 "Keep even-token write and partner zeroing in one pass without a destination read. Odd-token writes merge into the initialized pair." design.txt:277 "No packed slices or iterators; no generic row.set, set_pair, matrix.set, or owner expression constructor/assignment ... This scope decision removes the unneeded odd-boundary slice-write and temporary-slice lifetime questions." design.txt:297-301 write table: "Even cache append | No | Odd row becomes zero", "Odd cache append | Yes, pair must be initialized | Even row is preserved", "Direct element update | No read of other elements required | Other elements unchanged; this does not establish cache readiness". design.txt:303 "Production packed-V row writes use page::set_v or page::append_v. Both call the typed append/copy operations. Direct element mutation is useful for fixtures; it must not replace cache append."

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked for one sentence saying that a slice write must use the pair-preserving row path and that the no-read pair store is reserved for the full matrix and interior pairs. The revision removes the conflict at its source instead of adding the rule: writable slices, matrix.set(expr), row.set(expr) and set_pair are all out of the parent (277), so no write can start at an odd token or end at an even token except through append_v_row and copy_token, whose even path is the only no-read store and whose odd path reads and merges (229, 241, 243, 297-300). The remaining writable operation, single-element mutation through matrix[token][dimension], writes one bf16 element and touches no other element (218, 301), so it cannot erase a neighbor. This matches the only existing pair-write precedents, append_v's even paths zero the partner and its odd paths read-merge-write [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1866-1920 @f46e48bab498, file unchanged through 2880c3aa9b]. The verifier's extra case (a slice with an odd row count ending on an even row) is moot for the same reason. Grading on substance, the ambiguity no longer exists.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): Kind (d) omission, now filled. The narrowed round-1 recommendation asked for two statements: scaled_v_expr (the weighted V sum expression) keeps count as a separate constructor argument next to the typed V view, and the view's static 64-row shape is never a loop bound, with the 16-lane bound (count + 1) / 2 * 2 rows and the 8-lane bound count rows [r1-findings.md F42, verifier corrections]. The revision states both: "Keep scales, live-token count, and scratch as separate arguments. The 16-lane packed bound is (count + 1) / 2 * 2; the 8-lane row-major bound is count. Neither uses the view's static row count" [design.txt:257], and "Keep the live count separate from the storage shape. Keep pair rounding only in the 16-lane packed path; the 8-lane row-major path reads exactly count rows" [design.txt:316]. Every checkable fact matches the source: members const bf16s* const data; const size_t count; [kv_cache.hpp:1991-1993@f46e48bab498]; the 16-lane constructor takes (scales, data, count, scratch) and sets end = (count + 1) / 2 * 2 [kv_cache.hpp:2066-2078@f46e48bab498]; the 8-lane constructor takes the same four arguments and loops for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) [kv_cache.hpp:2139-2157@f46e48bab498]; page::scaled_v passes count() [kv_cache.hpp:2252-2262@f46e48bab498]; the supported widths 64/128/256/512 [design.txt:180] match the requires clause [kv_cache.hpp:2070-2071@f46e48bab498]. "Keep the page method" [design.txt:257] keeps the count() source implicitly, since the page method is what passes count() today. The verifiers' alternative (name the rule or poison rows beyond count+1 in the test) is met by the explicit rule "Neither uses the view's static row count". Correction: I agree with the checker's minor new defect and add the concrete hazard. design.txt:257 says "Give the expression constructor a typed packed V view", while the same page keeps V row-major in the 8-lane build [design.txt:270: "Keep row-major V in the 8-lane cache"; design.txt:322: "Keep native K and 8-lane V as their existing arrays"] and says page::v_tensor returns "the packed or row-major view selected by the build" [design.txt:255]. Read literally in the 8-lane build, line 257 would wrap row-major storage in a packed view, which reads the wrong layout; read cautiously, it leaves the 8-lane constructor's argument type unstated, and an implementer may keep the raw const bf16s* data [kv_cache.hpp:2139-2141@f46e48bab498], which contradicts "Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation" [design.txt:316]. Kind (c) ambiguity, minor. Fix: in design.txt:257 replace "a typed packed V view" with "the typed V view of the build (the type page::v_tensor returns): v_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, D> in the 16-lane build, the row-major const_view in the 8-lane build". The checker's optional residual (say count comes from page::count(); define or replace "live-token count", which is not in Words used here [design.txt:45 defines "Valid token row" instead]) is correct and stays optional.

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked the design to state the scratch rule itself and where it is written, instead of "preserve the child PR's existing rules"; the verifiers refined the rule to: the caller (gof::populate) owns a 64-byte-aligned scratch, one HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE slice per head, and the returned pointer is valid only until populate() reuses that slice for the next token position, citing gof.hpp and src/tron/gof.cpp at 30c4ac82cb. The revision states the rule in the child interface table [design.txt:381]: caller-owned, 64-byte-aligned, valid only until the scratch is reused, consume before the next token. Both citations check out. h/tron/gof.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:58-79 is struct page_info from its opening line through the v_head_fn declaration; line 66 says "the callback rebuilds the row in the caller-owned, 64-byte-aligned scratch and returns the scratch" and line 78 declares k_head_fn(slot, kv_head, bf16* scratch). src/tron/gof.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:203-220 is the alignas(64) k_scratch/v_scratch declarations (203-204) and the per-position loop that passes k_scratch.data() + h * HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE to k_head_fn (213) and consumes the returned pointers in k.set_position (218) before the loop's next iteration; line 220 closes the loop. The design's sentence "consumes the per-head rows before reusing the buffers for the next token" is an accurate plain-words reading of that code. The design also keeps S9 (main gof.hpp#L58-L66 at f46e48ba) for the parent's callback shape [design.txt:343]; that is right, because main's k_head_fn has no scratch parameter (gof.hpp@f46e48bab498:65 std::function<bf16*(kv_slot_id slot, size_t kv_head)> k_head_fn;). Round 1's concern that S9 did not show the child rule is met by adding S14 rather than changing S9. Small gaps, not defects: the caller is called "the caller" / "Hardware preparation" rather than gof::populate, and the "one HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE slice per head" detail is only in the linked source. Both are one click away through S14.

Still needed: Optional: in design.txt:381 replace "The caller owns" with "The caller, gof::populate (src/tron/gof.cpp), owns" so the implementer does not have to open the link to learn the caller's name.

Keep typed scaled_v_expr here unless a real include dependency requires a separate header." design.txt:252-256: page::set_v "Forward to append_v_row", page::get_v "call load_row", page::append_v "Keep the name; call copy_token." design.txt:196: "Keep the types in namespace tron". The round-1 hedge "Add a small internal header only if needed to prevent circular includes" no longer appears anywhere in design.txt (grep for "internal header" and "circular": no match).

Checker assessment: The round-1 finding was an ambiguity: the step that moves the V packing, unpacking and append code named no destination file, and an unmotivated "small internal header" hedge left the include direction open. The revision names the destination, h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp, in the step table (design.txt:352) and maps each moved body to its new operation by name (design.txt:241-243: set_v bodies -> append_v_row, get_v loops -> load_row, the four append_v parity branches -> copy_token). It keeps the page-level wrappers in kv_cache.hpp by name (design.txt:252-256), which matches the verifiers' point that the forwarding overloads at kv_cache.hpp:2474-2532@f46e48bab498 stay. The unmotivated hedge is gone; the remaining conditional at design.txt:353 concerns scaled_v_expr, names its default location and has a concrete trigger, so it is not the same defect. The include direction is fixed only in one direction in words ("No include of an attention kernel header", design.txt:352); that kv_cache.hpp includes vnni.hpp follows from step 2 using the owner, and no cycle is possible because kv_cache.hpp's current includes [kv_cache.hpp:24-32@f46e48bab498: common/numerics/bf16.hpp, system/memory.hpp, tron/kernels/expr.hpp, tron/models/common.hpp, tron/simd/auto.hpp, tron/simd/fp32.hpp, tron/simd/types.hpp, tron/tensor/slice.hpp, tron/tensor/tensor.hpp] contain nothing that a tensor-level header would need to include back. The verifiers said not to prescribe an exact include list, so its absence is not a gap. The namespace of the four free functions (append_v_row, load_row, copy_token, copy_plane) is not stated; design.txt:196 covers the types only. That is a small omission an implementer can resolve either way without building the wrong thing.

Still needed: Optional two clauses in step 1 (design.txt:352): "kv_cache.hpp includes this header; it includes nothing under h/tron/models/." and "The four bulk operations live in namespace tron (or tron::detail; state which)."

Resolved C09. Construction pass needs the slot-spec loop; allocate_kv_group has only a byte count (round-1 grade Note)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: checker: Resolved, source: Resolved, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design.txt:324-326: "// Default-initialize the array at its allocated address. // No parentheses or braces after the array bound. ::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[block_count];" design.txt:330: "Run the construction helper in book::allocate_kv_group after installing a successful allocation, before publishing access. Both initial allocation and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage use this path. Preserve the early return for zero-byte arenas." design.txt:331: "For uniform geometry, construct one array over the just-allocated arena's complete contiguous block region. Its bound is the checked arena byte count divided by sizeof(kv_block_t). This matches the existing uniform accessor's indexing across slots." design.txt:332: "For heterogeneous geometry, enumerate physical storage offsets once and select only slots in the just-allocated arena. Restoring the reclaimable arena must not restart objects in the retained arena. Use the slot specifications to choose each region's compile-time head width and head count. layout_t::storage_location identifies its arena; slot_base gives arena + n_pages * byte_offset. Construct geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks at that address. Do not construct the same region again for a logical alias." design.txt:333: "Include the physical EAGLE KV slot once, with the primary geometry. ... Construction cannot rely solely on the logical active-slot loop, which omits that extra physical slot. [C01] [C09]" design.txt:468: "F12 F40 F56 C01 C09 — Accepted; array extent clarified — Default-initialize actual block arrays. One array per uniform arena; one per heterogeneous physical slot."

Checker assessment: Round 1 (a note) asked the design to name the hooks for the construction pass: run it after allocate_kv_group succeeds, loop over physical storage offsets (including the EAGLE slot with the primary geometry), filter by layout_t::storage_location, place the array at slot_base, size it geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages (verifier correction 1), one array for the uniform case, skip zero-byte arenas, and name for_each_active_slot / fill_random as the precedent (verifier correction 3). The revision meets the substance, and each checkable claim is right at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b: allocate_kv_group returns early on bytes == 0 and installs the arena with destination.emplace [kv_cache.hpp:1199-1208]; both the constructor [:1101-1102] and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage [:968] call it, and publishing happens afterwards in refresh_kv_blocks_alias [:1114, :971]; storage_location returns {reclaimable, byte_offset} [:727-735]; slot_base returns arena->get() + n_pages * byte_offset with a checked multiply [:1188-1197]; each slot's block count is specs[slot].geometry.n_kv_heads * blocks per head [:664-666] and the accessor indexes blocks[kv_head * n_pages + pg] [:1334], so geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages per slot is right; the uniform accessor indexes one array across slots from kv_blocks_alias [:1284-1289], matching design.txt:331; the EAGLE slot is a physical offset beyond the logical slots with the primary geometry [:906-909, :1326-1329] and for_each_active_slot skips it [:1242-1249], matching design.txt:333. I also checked the hook's precondition: storage_slot_count_ and support_eagle_ are set in the constructor's initializer list [kv_cache.hpp:1090-1093] before the body calls allocate_kv_group [:1101], so a slot loop inside allocate_kv_group can read logical_slot_count() and has_eagle_storage() safely. On verifier correction (b) (do not implement as array placement-new): the design keeps ::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[block_count] (design.txt:326), which is the exact form the round-1 review page's edit list item 7 prescribed (prior-review.txt:1794). Per CWG 2382 (adopted in C++20; tron builds with CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23, CMakeLists.txt:56@2880c3aa9b), the non-allocating placement form may not add array overhead, and kv_block_t is trivially destructible, so no array cookie is needed under the Itanium ABI either. I do not count this as a defect. What is still unnamed: the loop bound storage_slot_count() [kv_cache.hpp:913-915], the EAGLE offset accessor eagle_storage_offset() [:906-909], and the fill_random precedent [:1058-1065]. The design links the code region that holds them and describes the loop precisely enough that an agent cannot guess wrong. Grade: resolved.

Still needed: Optional, one sentence in the design.txt:332-333 bullets: "Loop offsets 0 .. storage_slot_count() - 1 (kv_cache.hpp:913-915); the last one is eagle_storage_offset() when has_eagle_storage() (:906-909). fill_random (:1058-1065) shows the same active-slot loop plus EAGLE branch."

Every hook the revised design names checks out at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b: allocate_kv_group returns early on bytes == 0 and installs the arena with destination.emplace (:1199-1208, design.txt:330); the constructor calls it for retained then reclaimable (:1101-1102) and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage calls it (:968), with publication afterwards in refresh_kv_blocks_alias (:1114, :971), matching 'before publishing access'; storage_slot_count_ and support_eagle_ are set in the initializer list (:1090-1093) before the body calls allocate_kv_group, so a slot loop inside it can read logical_slot_count() and has_eagle_storage(); storage_location returns {reclaimable, byte_offset} (:727-735) and slot_base returns arena->get() + n_pages * byte_offset with a checked multiply (:1188-1197), matching design.txt:332; per-slot block count is n_kv_heads * block_bytes per page (:664-666) and the accessor indexes blocks[kv_head * n_pages + pg] (:1334), so 'geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks' is right; the uniform accessor indexes one array across slots over kv_blocks_alias (:1284-1289), matching design.txt:331, and the arena byte count is n_pages times a sum of whole blocks (:664-668, :1165), so 'arena bytes / sizeof(kv_block_t)' is an exact bound. Correction: One refinement to the checker's reasoning, no change to status or residual. The checker grounds the no-cookie claim on kv_block_t being trivially destructible. The Itanium ABI's rule for this exact case is stronger and does not depend on the destructor: section 2.7 says no cookie is required when the selected allocation function is the reserved placement allocation function, which ::new (void*) T[n] selects. Together with CWG 2382 (CD5, DR), the array form at design.txt:326 has zero overhead regardless of kv_block_t's destructor. The checker's optional one-sentence residual (loop bound storage_slot_count(), eagle_storage_offset(), fill_random precedent) is correct and remains optional.

Resolved F43. Typed kernel parameters pull SIMD headers into intrinsics-free header (round-1 grade Note)

Checker status: Resolved. Re-graders: checker: Resolved, source: Partly, fairness: Resolved.

Design text checked: design.txt:272: "Keep amx_attn_iface.hpp free of processor intrinsics. Forward-declare the packed view and the existing five-parameter view/const_view templates. Spell native dimensions and strides with std::integer_sequence, or share a small intrinsics-free declarations header." design.txt:273: "seq and sseq are aliases, not class templates that can be forward-declared. Do not repeat template defaults. Include complete tensor definitions only where callers or function definitions need them, including the fake AMX definitions. [Header-boundary finding]" design.txt:355 (step 4): "h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp, h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp, src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp | Use typed cache arguments. Keep the interface header free of intrinsics." design.txt:260-266 (kernel declarations): "void qk_rowmajor_128x4( const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> k_page, ..." / "void weights_times_v_128x4( v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> v_page, ...". design.txt:202-205: "template <size_t Rows, size_t Cols> using native_k_view = view<bf16, true, false, seq<Rows, Cols>>; template <size_t Rows, size_t Cols> using const_native_k_view = const_view<bf16, true, false, seq<Rows, Cols>>;". design.txt:475: "F43 | Accepted; declaration advice corrected | Keep the interface header intrinsics-free. seq and sseq are aliases; forward-declare the actual view classes with explicit shape and stride types."

Checker assessment: Round 1 asked the design to say how amx_attn_iface.hpp (the AMX kernel interface header, documented as containing no intrinsics) obtains the new parameter type names: forward-declare the view templates instead of including the tensor header, and include full headers only in amx_attn.cpp and the fake test translation units. The round-1 verifiers added that seq cannot be forward-declared (it is an alias template) and that the default Stride argument lives only in views.hpp, so a bare forward declaration cannot supply it. The revision adopts the forward-declaration route and incorporates both corrections. Every checkable claim holds. view and const_view are five-parameter templates with a defaulted fifth parameter, Stride = row_major<Dim> [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp:22-36 @2880c3aa9b]. seq and sseq are alias templates over std::integer_sequence [h/tron/tensor/seq.hpp:22 and 25 @2880c3aa9b], so "seq and sseq are aliases" is right, and spelling them as std::integer_sequence<size_t,...> and std::integer_sequence<ptrdiff_t,...> names the same types. row_major<seq<64,128>> is sseq<128,1> [seq.hpp:388-394 and the static_assert at 510-511 @2880c3aa9b], so an explicit stride spelling is possible. "Do not repeat template defaults" is the C++ rule; g++ 11.4 on this host rejects a repeated default with "redefinition of default argument for 'class U'", and accepts a bare forward declaration followed by a definition that adds the default. A forward-declared class is a valid by-value parameter type in a function declaration (confirmed with g++ 11.4), so the kernel declarations at design.txt:260-266 compile against forward declarations. expr.hpp:17-22 @2880c3aa9b already forward-declares view and const_view without the default, which is the precedent round 1 named. amx_attn_iface.hpp already includes common/numerics/bf16.hpp [amx_attn_iface.hpp:112 @f46e48bab498], so the name bf16 is available there. With forward declarations the header comment "contains no intrinsics" [amx_attn_iface.hpp:2-5 @f46e48bab498] and the "// intrinsics-free" tag [self_attention.hpp:21 @2880c3aa9b] stay accurate, so no comment update is needed. One note, no change required: seq.hpp itself is intrinsics-free (its includes are <algorithm>, <type_traits>, <utility>, common/assert.hpp, common/attributes.hpp, common/numerics/std.hpp @2880c3aa9b, none of which pulls tron/simd.hpp), so amx_attn_iface.hpp may include tron/tensor/seq.hpp and write seq<>/sseq<> directly instead of spelling std::integer_sequence; the design's second option, a shared declarations header, covers this.

source re-grader (Partly): The revision does answer the round-1 omission (how amx_attn_iface.hpp, the AMX kernel interface header, gets the parameter type names): forward-declare the packed view and the five-parameter view/const_view templates, spell shape and stride with std::integer_sequence or share a small intrinsics-free declarations header, do not repeat template defaults (design.txt:272-273). Every C++ fact in it checks out: view and const_view are five-parameter templates with Stride = row_major<Dim> defaulted [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp:22-36 @2880c3aa9b]; seq and sseq are alias templates [h/tron/tensor/seq.hpp:21-25 @2880c3aa9b]; expr.hpp:17-22 @2880c3aa9b is the forward-declaration precedent; amx_attn_iface.hpp:1-5 @f46e48bab498 documents "no intrinsics" and line 112 already includes common/numerics/bf16.hpp; self_attention.hpp:21 @2880c3aa9b carries the "// intrinsics-free" tag. But the round-1 verifier correction (b) asked the design to pick one route AND make the const_native_k_view alias consistent with it, and the revision does not. Three statements cannot be followed together: the alias is defined with four arguments, relying on the default Stride (design.txt:202-205); the sample kernel declaration inside the interface header uses that alias, const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> (design.txt:260-261); and line 272 says to forward-declare without the default and spell strides with std::integer_sequence. Compile probes with g++ 11.4 (the only compiler on this host; the pinned clang 19 is absent, so clang behaviour is Insufficient data): (a) the four-argument alias after a bare five-parameter forward declaration fails, "wrong number of template arguments (4, should be 5)"; (b) an alias named const_native_k_view spelled with std::integer_sequence<ptrdiff_t, C, 1> next to the tensor header's four-argument alias fails, "conflicting declaration of template"; (c) an alias spelled row_major<seq<R,C>> coexists with the four-argument alias, and a forward-declared class works as a by-value parameter with the default added later. self_attention.hpp includes both amx_attn_iface.hpp (line 21) and kv_cache.hpp (line 27) @2880c3aa9b, so any TU including it would see both spellings. An implementing agent following line 272 literally therefore hits a compile error at the first build. Kind (c) ambiguity, severity minor (caught by the compiler, not a wrong design). Because this is the exact point round 1 raised, I grade F43 partly rather than resolved plus a separate new defect. Correction: Fold the checker's "new defect" into F43's residual instead of listing it separately, and sharpen it with the probe result: spelling the stride as std::integer_sequence<ptrdiff_t, Cols, 1> under the alias name const_native_k_view conflicts with the four-argument alias (g++ 11.4: "conflicting declaration of template"), while row_major<seq<Rows, Cols>> does not. Recommended text for design.txt:272-273: define native_k_view and const_native_k_view exactly once, in one intrinsics-free declarations header that includes tron/tensor/seq.hpp (its includes are <algorithm>, <type_traits>, <utility>, common/assert.hpp, common/attributes.hpp and common/numerics/std.hpp @2880c3aa9b, none of which reaches tron/simd.hpp), forward-declares view, const_view and v_vnni_view without defaults, and spells the stride as row_major<seq<Rows, Cols>>; state that both h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp and h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp include that header; and remove the "std::integer_sequence" option from line 272, or limit it to function parameter types, never to the alias name.

fairness re-grader (Resolved): Round 1 asked the design to say how amx_attn_iface.hpp (the AMX kernel interface header, whose comment says it contains no intrinsics) obtains the new parameter type names, and the verifiers added that seq cannot be forward-declared and that a bare forward declaration of view/const_view cannot supply the default Stride argument [r1-findings.md F43 Recommendation and Verifier corrections]. The revision adopts forward declarations and both corrections [design.txt:272-273; step 4 at design.txt:355]. Every checkable claim holds at live main 2880c3aa9b. view and const_view are five-parameter struct templates with Stride = row_major<Dim> as default [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp:22-36]. seq and sseq are alias templates over std::integer_sequence [h/tron/tensor/seq.hpp:21-25], so "seq and sseq are aliases" is right. row_major<seq<R,C>> expands to sseq<C,1> [seq.hpp:387-394, static_assert at 510-511], so an explicit stride spelling exists. The precedent forward declarations without the default are at h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:17-22. The header comment "contains no intrinsics" is unchanged at amx_attn_iface.hpp:2-5, the header includes common/numerics/bf16.hpp at line 112, its kernels are still raw-pointer at lines 219-233, and self_attention.hpp:21 still carries "// intrinsics-free" (all @2880c3aa9b). I compiled the C++ rules with g++ 11.4 from stdin (no files written): a repeated default after a forward declaration that already has one is rejected ("redefinition of default argument"), which supports design.txt:273; a bare forward declaration followed by a definition that adds the default compiles; a five-argument alias plus a by-value parameter of the still-incomplete view type in a function declaration compiles, so the signatures at design.txt:260-266 are valid against forward declarations. seq.hpp includes only <algorithm>, <type_traits>, <utility>, common/assert.hpp, common/attributes.hpp and common/numerics/std.hpp [seq.hpp:3-9], so it is itself intrinsics-free, as the checker notes. Note only: design.txt:475 says "view classes" while view and const_view are declared with struct [views.hpp:27, 36]; a class-key mismatch compiles, and clang only warns under -Wmismatched-tags. The checker's new minor defect (the design never says which header defines native_k_view and const_native_k_view) is real: grep of design.txt finds those names only at lines 203, 205 and 261, and step 1 at design.txt:352 assigns only the V types to h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp. Correction: The checker's new defect stands, but its "Insufficient data" on whether the two alias spellings can coexist is too cautious: g++ 11.4 already rejects them. I compiled (from stdin) a forward declaration of const_view, the explicit five-argument alias the design suggests at design.txt:272, then the full const_view definition with its default, then the four-argument alias from design.txt:205; g++ reports "conflicting declaration of template ... const_native_k_view" because the two alias bodies are not token-equivalent before the dependent default is substituted. So any translation unit that includes both amx_attn_iface.hpp (with the explicit alias) and the tensor header (with the four-argument alias), which self_attention.hpp does today via kv_cache.hpp [self_attention.hpp:21, 27 @2880c3aa9b], fails to compile. I also confirmed the other half: after a bare forward declaration the four-argument alias fails with "wrong number of template arguments (4, should be 5)". Recommendation unchanged from the checker: name one header (the "small intrinsics-free declarations header" the design already offers at design.txt:272) that holds the forward declarations of view, const_view and v_vnni_view plus the two native-K aliases, defined exactly once with the stride spelled explicitly or with tron/tensor/seq.hpp included, and state that both amx_attn_iface.hpp and h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp include it. Severity minor is fair: a violation is caught at compile time, not built wrongly.

Major N01. Both-chunk-width rule forces unused 8-lane packed bodies

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity major). Every evidence citation in N01 holds at live main 2880c3aa9b and in design.txt. Verified: (1) design.txt:270 says verbatim "Compile all three packed V types under both TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 8 and == 16. Derive a pair chunk's width from chunk_size." and the section 9 F11 row (design.txt:467) records "both chunk widths"; design.txt:220 states the row.chunk(i) contract in chunk_size terms ("pair_base + 2 * chunk_size * i"). (2) design.txt:352 (step 1) says "Keep the existing vector bodies here"; the existing bodies are 16-lane-only: kv_cache.hpp:2281 #if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 opens the set_v/get_v definitions, and 2289-2320 use _mm512_cvtepu16_epi32, _mm512_store_si512, _mm512_ternarylogic_epi32 with i += 16. No sentence in the design says whether the operation bodies may stay 16-lane-only (grep of design.txt for AVX2/_mm256/guard/"only under" finds nothing about packed bodies). So the conflict/ambiguity between 270 and 352 is real. (3) Class completeness is the only 8-lane requirement: design.txt:265-267 passes v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> v_page by value; t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:166-190 defines the fakes outside any #ifdef (the TEST_CASE at 192 is inside #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, the fakes are not) and weights_times_v_128x4(const bf16*, const float*, size_t, float* output) never dereferences the plane argument; t/CMakeLists.txt:596 registers t_amx_dispatch_dtype unconditionally. C++ [temp.inst]: implicit instantiation of a class template specialization instantiates member declarations, not member definitions, and this matches the round-1 F11 verifier correction. bf16x32 = __m512i is defined unconditionally (simd/types.hpp:25-27, outside the #ifdef TRON_AVX512_ENABLED at 42), so an unguarded 16-lane member body parses at 8 lanes and fails only if instantiated. (4) No 8-lane production caller exists: self_attention.hpp:30-35 #error when TRON_AMX_DISPATCH is defined with TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16; both kernel calls (1654 qk_rowmajor_128x4, 1680-1682 weights_times_v_128x4 over pg.template v_data<geometry.kv>(...)) sit inside #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH at 1571-1701. The 8-lane cache keeps row-major V (kv_cache.hpp:2199-2201 bf16s v[page_size][head_size / chunk_size]; design.txt:322), the 8-lane save uses pg.template v<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head, j).set(slice...) (model.hpp:2833-2837), and the 8-lane append is a memcpy (kv_cache.hpp:1947-1955). (5) Section 8 test rows (design.txt:395-399) carry no chunk guard, and the 8-lane row (design.txt:413) expects test execution ("Establish the unmodified-baseline result before attributing a failure to the parent"). Three corrections, none a refutation: (a) "forces"/"makes the implementing agent write AVX2 bodies" over-states; the design leaves the body question open (270 vs 352), it does not mandate 8-lane bodies. (b) "t_llama_unit would instantiate the bodies at 8 lanes" holds only for rows that build a packed owner directly (396 bits/conversions, 398 expression reads); row 395 goes through page::set_v, which at 8 lanes forwards to the row-major .set() (design.txt:254, 180) and instantiates no packed body. (c) The recommendation "mark the 8-lane row as a compile-only check" is wrong guidance: the parent changes 8-lane code (typed set_v wrapper 254, v_tensor accessor and v_data/v_base removal 255, typed scaled_v_expr constructor 257), so the existing row-major cases must still run at 8 lanes. A native-derived expectation for the generic path fails the weekly coverage lane, which builds the Debug coverage preset and runs the host tests (README.ci.md:555-557@2880c3aa9b; cpp-coverage.yml:4-5, 59@2880c3aa9b make build-coverage; GNUmakefile:615-616). The repository already records this trap for an existing test (t/t_bf16.cpp:97-99@2880c3aa9b: "this test may fail ... if IGNORE_NAN is set"). Severity: major. The section-8 "Bits and conversions" row cannot be implemented for NaN inputs as written without the missing guidance, and the fix is the one added sentence plus the test-row guard that N02 recommends.

Minor M01. t_llama_unit itself does not compile in the 8-lane configuration at unmodified main

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). Words used here: t_llama_unit = the cache and model unit-test program; 8-lane build = TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 8, the AVX2 build with 8 fp32 values per vector; page::set_v / page::get_v = the packed-V write and read methods of the KV page class. CORE CLAIM CONFIRMED from primary sources (no compile run, per the rules). TRON_CHUNK_SIZE is 8 whenever TRON_AVX512_ENABLED is undefined [h/tron/simd/auto.hpp@2880c3aa9b:17-21]. TRON_AVX512_ENABLED is defined only inside if(AVX512) [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:269-272], so -DAVX512=OFF does give the 8-lane build. page::set_v and page::get_v are declared only inside #if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 and defined only inside a second such block [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1616-1674 and 2281-2532]. The #else branch declares only v() and v_ptr() [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1674-1725]. No other header or source defines set_v or get_v (git grep -E '\b(set_v|get_v)\s*\(' 2880c3aa9b -- h/ src/ matches only kv_cache.hpp), so no base class supplies them. The two sites the finding names are real and unguarded: the requires-expression at t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:105-109 asks for page.get_v with a bf16* and is asserted true at :483 with STATIC_REQUIRE, which is a static_assert (no CATCH_CONFIG_RUNTIME_STATIC_REQUIRE anywhere in the repo at 2880c3aa9b); check_wide_scaled_v calls page->template set_v<geometry> at :142 and is instantiated unconditionally at :1199-1205. The preprocessor guards in the file are exactly the six blocks the finding lists (:4-6 is an unrelated _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS guard). t_llama_unit is registered unconditionally [t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:586-592]. heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:443 calls page->set_v<software_geometry.kv> on the concrete heterogeneous_model::book inside a non-template SECTION, so it also fails at 8 lanes. WHAT THE FINDING GETS WRONG (partly right, not refuted). The recommendation (keep the fill, list it in the search, name it in the definition of done) therefore moves the design toward a complete raw-access inventory, not away from Ben's request. Consequence is bounded: fill_storage_slot compiles unchanged once the owner replaces the bf16s v[...] array (kv_cache.hpp:2198 today) because sizeof(block)/sizeof(bf16) is unchanged, and both tests pass whether the agent leaves it or wraps it; the cost is an unsettled decision and a possible over-zealous rewrite of a helper whose purpose is to bypass the partner-zero rule. That matches minor (should change, low risk), not major and not note.

Minor N13. bf16_chunk 'different signature silently selects conversion' is wrong

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). I re-derived both claims from the primary sources and the finding holds. Claim 1 (design.txt:221, "a different signature can silently select conversion instead"). The expression base decides by comparing member-function pointers: if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk) [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:110-117@2880c3aa9b]. Consumers call through the base reference (dmatensor(expr<B, N> const& rhs) ... rhs.bf16_chunk(i)) [h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:270-276 and 291-296@2880c3aa9b], so that comparison is instantiated for any new row type. When B declares no member named bf16_chunk, &B::bf16_chunk names the inherited base member, the pointers are equal, and the fp32 conversion branch is chosen with no diagnostic. When B declares a same-named member with a different function type, there is no composite pointer type, so the comparison is ill-formed (C++ [expr.type]/4, no clause covers different function types). I confirmed this with g++ 11.4 -fsyntax-only on a minimal copy of the expr pattern (stdin, nothing written): omitted member and differently named member -> fallback branch taken silently; non-const, int parameter, different return type, overload set, member template, and static member -> compile errors ("comparison between distinct pointer types ... lacks a cast", "address of overloaded function with no contextual type information", "invalid operands"). The existing overrides in tron use exactly the plain form: bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t i) const noexcept [h/tron/hardware/permuted.hpp:53@2880c3aa9b] and the same with a requires clause [h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:366-368@2880c3aa9b]. So the design sentence misstates the failure mode: a different signature is loud, and only omission (or a different name) is silent. Claim 2 (design.txt:398, "silently takes a lossy fallback"). The fallback is fp32s_to_bf16s(self().chunk(i)) [expr.hpp:115@2880c3aa9b]. fp32s_to_bf16s ORs 0x00010000 only where the exponent field equals 0x7f800000 AND the low 16 bits are nonzero, then shifts right 16 and narrows [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:92-109@f46e48bab498 for 16 lanes; :55-88 for 8 lanes uses the same mask then keeps bytes 2-3 of each lane]. The design's own chunk(i) contract produces fp32 lanes from the packed bf16 pair by even_part (shift left 16) or odd_part (mask the high 16 bits) [design.txt:220 and :225; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2000-2007@2880c3aa9b], so the low 16 bits of every lane are zero and the NaN correction never fires. The fallback therefore returns the stored bf16 bits unchanged; it costs instructions, not bits. The section 8 check "exact bf16 copies with independent patterns" (design.txt:398) cannot detect an omitted override, and the objdump inspection list at design.txt:440 does not name bf16_chunk extraction. Round-1 F35 verifier corrections stated both points ("Omitting the member entirely is the only way to get the silent fp32 round trip; a mismatched parameter, return type, or const-qualifier fails ... as a compile error"; "That fallback is bit-exact for stored bf16 values ... so the design's ... check does not detect the omission") [r1-findings.md:341-352, F35 entry]. The revised design's section 9 lists F35 as "Accepted with concrete contracts ... exact bf16 override" [design.txt:467] but kept the wrong failure mode. The finding's proposed static_assert is sound: with the member omitted, decltype(&v_vnni_row<...>::bf16_chunk) is a pointer to member of the expr base, which std::is_same_v does not equate with a pointer to member of v_vnni_row, so the assertion fires. Two small corrections to the finding text, neither of which rescues the design sentence: (1) the word "repeats" is wrong; the original design row read "matrix[token].bf16_chunk(i) | Extract the stored bf16 bits directly. Avoid a float conversion during exact copies." [original design-text.txt:260] and had neither the "different signature" sentence nor "lossy fallback", so both sentences were introduced by the revision (as R90 and R69 say). (2) "A missing noexcept still compares unequal and the override is used" follows the standard's composite-pointer-type rule ([expr.type]/4.6), but g++ 11.4 rejects that comparison ("comparison between distinct pointer types ... lacks a cast"); tron builds with clang 19 (facts-r2.md toolchain line), which I could not run here (no clang on this host). Either outcome is a compile-time result, not a silent fallback, so the finding's conclusion is unaffected.

Minor N15. Aligned flag of moved set_v/get_v row views unstated

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). I re-derived every cited fact from the primary sources at live main 2880c3aa9b and from the revised design text. Source facts confirmed (kv_cache.hpp is unchanged from c7844ca2ce through 2880c3aa9b, per facts-r2.md): - set_v (the V row save) loads the caller's source with aligned-form intrinsics: _mm256_load_epi32(vout_ptr + i) for bf16 [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2300, 2308@2880c3aa9b] and fp16 [:2339, 2349], _mm512_load_ps(vout_ptr + i) for float [:2380, 2389]. get_v (the V row read) stores the caller's destination with aligned-form intrinsics: _mm512_store_ps [:2421, 2430], _mm256_store_si256 [:2455, 2463]. - tron's row view has a bool aligned template flag [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:115-117@2880c3aa9b], and the flag selects aligned vs unaligned loads/stores in the chunk helpers (tron_mm_load_ps vs tron_mm_loadu_ps, tron_mm_load_bf16 vs tron_mm_loadu_bf16) [h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:32-45, 53-68@2880c3aa9b]. [model.hpp:2834-2836]. What the revised design says. The no-relabel rule is stated once, in the contract table row "View copy / conversion": "No public pointer constructor, .data member, or pointer conversion for packed views." [design.txt:222]. The only type the design calls a view is v_vnni_view: "v_vnni_view accesses a packed V matrix. v_vnni_row reads one logical row." [design.txt:43]. Section 5 itself uses "view" and "row" as two different objects: "The row stores its pair address and even/odd position by value. It remains valid after a temporary view object disappears" [design.txt:212]. The word "friend" appears once in the whole design, for detail::vnni_access (the internal raw-pointer accessor) [design.txt:223]; the design never says that v_vnni_view is a friend of v_vnni_row or that the row's constructor is private (grep of design.txt for friend, private, constructor, relabel: lines 61, 63, 212, 222, 223, 277 only). Line 61 "restricted construction of views" has the same "views" wording. The generic Words row "A view accesses those values without owning their storage" could be read to include the row, but that reading conflicts with the design's own row-versus-view usage at line 212, so it does not remove the ambiguity. Why an implementing agent would guess wrong. The design tells the implementer to keep the row's aliases "consistent with existing views" [design.txt:213]. The existing tron rank-1 view is a struct with a public pointer member T* data; and a public constructor explicit constexpr view(T* data = nullptr) noexcept : data(data) {} [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:116-126 @f46e48bab498]. The rank-2 view builds its row as return element(data + s0 * i); [view.hpp:72-75 @f46e48bab498]. Copying that pattern gives v_vnni_row a public (pointer, parity) constructor and a public data member. Why the harm is real. The design gives writable rows writable element access: "Non-const writable access changes only that element." [design.txt:218]. With a public (pair address, parity) constructor, v_vnni_row<bf16,D>(ptr, false)[i] = x writes ptr[2*i] through any pointer, which is exactly the relabelling Ben's rule forbids: "The private constructor prevents routine callers from relabelling an arbitrary row-major pointer as packed data." [Ben comment 5765866077, github-review.json]. Ben's sketch has no row type at all (no operator[]), so the row is the design's own addition and the rule reaches it only if the design says so. Not already handled. No round-1 finding covers the row's constructor: r1-findings.md mentions v_vnni_row only for the rename (F-naming), const-row indexing (view.hpp:146 precedent), the bf16_chunk override, and the child's k_vnni_row write rule. Section 9 of the design therefore makes no claim about it. Severity check: minor is right. The fix is one sentence in the contract table; production code paths (append_v_row, load_row, copy_token) are unaffected; the risk is a silent breach of Ben's access rule that a reviewer would catch late. One nuance for the recommendation: a const v_vnni_view<bf16,R,D> must produce v_vnni_row<const bf16,D> [design.txt:218 "Const matrix access yields a read-only row"], so the friend declaration must cover the whole v_vnni_view family (all T), not one instantiation.

The general retain list says "restricted construction of views" [design.txt:61]. The row is described only as "v_vnni_row reads one logical row" [design.txt:43], "v_vnni_row<T,D> inherits expr<row_type,D>" [design.txt:211], and "The row stores its pair address and even/odd position by value" [design.txt:212]. Severity minor is right: one added sentence fixes it, and the risk is a small leak in encapsulation rather than wrong behavior.

Minor N25. EAGLE bullet omits uniform-geometry requirement; misread as heterogeneous

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). I re-derived every factual claim of N25 from kv_cache.hpp at live main 2880c3aa9b (the file is unchanged from c7844ca2ce, so the same lines hold at f46e48ba and 98bb8cb2) and from the revised design text. All hold. (1) EAGLE requires uniform geometry: kv_cache.hpp:771 static constexpr bool eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0;; :788-789 TRON_ASSERT(!support_eagle || eagle_compatible, "EAGLE cache views require uniform geometry and embedding storage");; :1158-1159 if (support_eagle && (!eagle_compatible || logical_slot_count == 0)) return std::nullopt; inside calculate_allocation_sizes, which the constructor calls at :1096-1098 and returns on nullopt. So a heterogeneous layout with EAGLE can never allocate. (2) The EAGLE slot lives at the end of the retained arena and is covered by the uniform whole-arena array: arena_sizes :716-719 sets result = offsets.values[logical_slot_count] then adds offsets.values[1].total() to result.retained when support_eagle; storage_location :727-735 gives reclaimable = offset.i < logical_slot_count && ... so the EAGLE offset (== logical_slot_count, eagle_storage_offset :906-909) resolves to prefix.retained of the retained arena; slot_base :1188-1197 multiplies by n_pages. make_kv_slot_offsets :654-676 sizes each slot as n_kv_heads * block_bytes per page, so the retained byte count is a whole number of kv_block_t and the design's "checked arena byte count divided by sizeof(kv_block_t)" (design.txt:331) spans the EAGLE slot too. The uniform accessor :1288-1289 indexes one kv_block_t array from kv_blocks_alias, matching the design's rule. (3) Restore never reconstructs the EAGLE slot: restore_reclaimable_kv_storage :963-968 calls allocate_kv_group(/*reclaimable=*/true, ...) only. (4) The revised design omits the precondition: grep -i eagle over design.txt hits only lines 28, 306, 333, 353, 399, 468; none says EAGLE requires uniform geometry, none says the EAGLE slot sits in the retained arena. The bullets run uniform (331), heterogeneous (332), EAGLE (333) in that order, and the section 9 row (468) repeats the same order: "One array per uniform arena; one per heterogeneous physical slot. Include EAGLE KV, exclude embeddings." Round-1 C01 recommended "(EAGLE requires uniform geometry, so the retained arena is one kv_block array)" and its verifier correction (a)/(b) asked for the retained-arena placement and the constructor-only construction [r1-findings.md:106-111]; the revision added "once" and "with the primary geometry" but not those three statements. Because line 333 never names the arena holding the EAGLE slot, a reader cannot connect line 332's "must not restart objects in the retained arena" to EAGLE. Severity minor stands: the omission cannot produce a wrong build (an EAGLE branch in the heterogeneous path is unreachable, and the uniform array already covers the slot), but the implementer must rediscover the precondition, the arena placement and the constructor-only lifetime from the source.
    Correction: One refinement, not a refutation. The finding says the bullet's caution about "the logical active-slot loop" applies to a loop the design does not prescribe. The caution is still correct and useful: for_each_active_slot (kv_cache.hpp:1243-1249) iterates only slot < logical_slot_count() over slot_specs and cannot reach the EAGLE offset, and fill_random (:1060-1064) needs a separate fill_storage_slot<layout_t::primary_geometry>(eagle_storage_offset(), ...) call; round-1 C09's verifier correction named exactly that for_each_active_slot + EAGLE pattern as the precedent to reuse. N25's recommended rewrite drops the caution; keep it, qualified as in R09 ("if the implementer uses a per-offset loop for uniform layouts too, it must run over offsets 0 .. storage_slot_count_ - 1 and include eagle_storage_offset() with layout_t::primary_geometry; for_each_active_slot omits it"). Add to the rewrite that the EAGLE slot is the last primary-geometry slot of the RETAINED arena (:727-735, :716-719) and is constructed only in the constructor because restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena (:968); without the arena placement the reader cannot link line 332's retained-arena sentence to EAGLE.

Include EAGLE KV, exclude embeddings."). None says EAGLE exists only with uniform geometry, and none says the EAGLE slot lives in the retained arena. The source facts the finding cites are correct at live main 2880c3aa9b (kv_cache.hpp unchanged since c7844ca2ce per facts-r2.md): :771 static constexpr bool eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0;; :788-789 TRON_ASSERT(!support_eagle || eagle_compatible, "EAGLE cache views require uniform geometry and embedding storage");; :1158-1159 if (support_eagle && (!eagle_compatible || logical_slot_count == 0)) return std::nullopt;; :717-719 arena_sizes adds offsets.values[1].total() to result.retained; :731-734 storage_location returns reclaimable = offset.i < logical_slot_count && ..., so the EAGLE offset (== logical_slot_count, :908) is never reclaimable; :968 restore_reclaimable_kv_storage calls allocate_kv_group(/*reclaimable=*/true, ...) only. The constructor (:1095-1097) returns before any allocate_kv_group call when calculate_allocation_sizes returns nullopt, so a heterogeneous book asked for EAGLE never gets an arena and the construction helper never runs for it. Therefore the heterogeneous enumeration of design.txt:332 can never meet an EAGLE slot, and under the uniform rule of design.txt:331 (one array over the whole just-allocated arena, bound = arena bytes / sizeof(kv_block_t)) the retained-arena array already covers the EAGLE slot. The finding is not an attack on a deliberate choice: round-1 C01's recommendation and its verifier correction (a) asked to state "EAGLE requires uniform geometry, so the retained arena is one kv_block array" and (b) to state that restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena so the EAGLE slot is constructed once in the constructor [r1-findings.md C01]. The revision added "Include the physical EAGLE KV slot once, with the primary geometry" (design.txt:333) and marks C01 "Accepted" (design.txt:468), but adopted neither (a) nor a plain form of (b); "once" alone does not say the slot is retained-only. Severity minor is right, not major: an implementing agent following design.txt:331-332 builds correct storage either way, and the worst outcome is an unreachable EAGLE branch inside the heterogeneous enumeration, which a reviewer would flag but which cannot break the build or the cache.

The constructor allocates retained then reclaimable at lines 1101-1102. So the EAGLE slot is constructed only in the constructor. - Under uniform geometry every slot region is n_kv_heads * sizeof(kv_block_t) bytes per page (make_kv_slot_offsets lines 651-672), so a whole-arena array covers the EAGLE slot; the existing uniform accessor already indexes one array across slots from kv_blocks_alias (lines 1288-1289). - The "logical active-slot loop" the bullet warns about is for_each_active_slot (lines 1245-1251); its only construction-like precedent, fill_random (lines 1059-1064), adds a separate EAGLE call. Design facts: - design.txt:331-333 are three sibling <li> items in one list (HTML lines 266-268), so the EAGLE bullet reads as an instruction for both branches. The heterogeneous bullet says "Use the slot specifications to choose each region's compile-time head width and head count" (design.txt:332). slot_specs has no EAGLE entry (kv_cache.hpp:784-786 "The extra physical storage has no logical descriptor"; :1326-1329 uses layout_t::primary_geometry). An agent honoring "Include the physical EAGLE KV slot once, with the primary geometry" in that branch must add a special case that is unreachable. - The design nowhere states that EAGLE requires uniform geometry: grep "uniform" in design.txt hits only lines 87, 331, 468. The Words row (design.txt:28) is unchanged from round 1. - Round-1 C01 asked for exactly the missing sentences: "(EAGLE requires uniform geometry, so the retained arena is one kv_block array)" and "Restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena, so the EAGLE slot is constructed once, in the constructor" (r1-findings.md, C01 recommendation and verifier correction items (a) and (b)). Section 9 (design.txt:468) marks C01 "Accepted" with only "Include EAGLE KV, exclude embeddings". The two-buffer ambiguity of C01 IS resolved by "Do not touch x_data" (design.txt:333). The uniform-geometry precondition and the constructed-once point are not. Intent lens: Ben's comment #3 asks that "The page arena must construct the actual storage type" with no "implicit clearing to hot allocation paths" (facts-r1.md:28). The finding's recommendation keeps construction in allocate_kv_group and only says which branch covers the EAGLE slot; it does not move the design away from Ben's requirement. jhan's prompt says "Another agent will implement the design by reading this file" (codex-add-tensor-type.md, output section), so ambiguity for the implementing agent is the correct standard. Consequence: an implementing agent following the text as written may (a) add an unreachable EAGLE branch to the heterogeneous enumeration, or (b) construct the EAGLE region a second time in the uniform path after the whole-arena array. Neither produces a wrong build, and the parent PR can still merge, so this is not major. It is more than a note because the revision's disposition of C01 is incomplete and the implementing agent must guess which branch the bullet belongs to. Severity minor stands. Small refinement, not a correction: R09's clause is worth keeping in the rewrite: if an implementer uses the per-offset loop for uniform layouts too, the loop must run over offsets 0 .. storage_slot_count_ - 1 and use layout_t::primary_geometry for eagle_storage_offset() (kv_cache.hpp:906-909, 1326-1329).

Minor N31. K token lane sentence imprecise: one lane per line, 64 lines

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). I re-derived the layout from the child's source and the finding holds. Design sentence, verified verbatim in the HTML and in design.txt:383: "A K token owns separate 4-byte lanes in a shared cache line." Plural "lanes", singular "line". The literal reading is that one token owns several 4-byte lanes inside one 64-byte line. Child layout at h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6: the index formula at lines 25-26 is plane[(((s*4+c)*16+dp)*16+t)*2+j]. The 64-byte line index is (s*4+c)*16+dp. For one token (fixed c, t), s takes 4 values and dp takes 16 values, so the token's 128 dimensions fall in 64 distinct lines, and inside each line the token occupies dword position t only. Lines 16-17 say "One 64-byte row holds that dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens". Lines 28-29 say "Token i owns column (i % 16) of token block (i / 16) in every panel". The store_block comment at line 191 says "every one of the block's 64 lines receives 16 partial writes". The child's gof.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:69-70 says "One 64-byte line holds that 4-byte unit for 16 tokens, so a token's 128 values sit in 64 lines". So a token owns exactly one 4-byte lane per line, in 64 lines, and 16 tokens share every line. The design sentence states the opposite arrangement (several lanes of one token in one line). The finding's factual claim is right. The finding's other evidence also checks out: scatter_row (k_vnni.hpp:139-146) is a loop of 4 _mm512_i32scatter_epi32 calls with scale DWORD_BYTES_4; store_block's partial path (line 212) uses _mm512_mask_storeu_epi32 with the present mask; common.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:1060-1062 reads "Their writers touch disjoint token lanes (masked stores). So two threads may write one block without conflict." (exact quote, correct file). Attempted refutation: one could read "separate" as "separate from other tokens' lanes" with "a shared cache line" as a generic singular. That reading is possible but not the natural one given the plural/singular mismatch, and the finding already frames the defect as an imprecision, not a false design decision. The design's own formula (design.txt:172-178) and the [S10] link let a careful reader recover the truth, which lowers the risk but does not make the sentence correct. Nothing in the primary sources supports the sentence as written. Severity stays minor: the design asks the implementer to keep this contract "alongside Note [K VNNI storage]" (design.txt:383), so the wrong sentence could be copied into a code comment; low risk because the linked source and the design's own index formula contradict it. The recommended replacement ("one 4-byte lane (two consecutive dimensions) in each of 64 cache lines. Sixteen tokens share every line.") matches k_vnni.hpp exactly (4 steps x 16 pair rows = 64 lines; BLOCK_TOKENS_16 = 16 tokens per line). Minor citation correction only: the finding cites "Token i owns column" at k_vnni.hpp:29-30; it is at lines 28-29. Immaterial.

Facts: no child code reads a VNNI-K row through expr (dense and partial QK take the whole plane [self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1437-1439, 1635-1639]; the software loop states "no row view" for VNNI slots [:1594-1603]; staging uses get_k_row [full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2655]; copies use gather_row + scatter_row [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2111]; all tests use set_k_row/get_k_row), and a K row chunk would be an 8-line dword gather. Corrections to the finding's argument: design.txt:63 keeps expression reads and defers only slices, iteration, generic assignment and expression constructors, so it does not support deferring a K row expression; the design mandates the K row expression for uniformity with V under Ben's comment #2 ("uniform interface based upon expr"), recorded as a decision at design.txt:56 and as an open question to Ben at design.txt:84; V's row expression likewise has no production caller and was kept by round-1 F08 as the cheap "usual tensor operation"; round-1 C05 recommended a k_vnni_row with expr<row, D>. Corrected recommendation: in child item 4 (design.txt:369), tie the K row expression to Ben's answer on the operator[]/expr question (design.txt:84). If Ben accepts expr access, keep it and add one sentence: k_vnni_row::chunk() is an inspection/test read (one dword gather across 8 lines per 16 dimensions, built from the gather_row pattern), and hot paths (staging, page copies, QK) use load_row, store_row, store_block and the whole-plane kernel arguments, never the row expression. If Ben declines expr access, drop the K row expression together with V's. Either way, state the choice; do not leave "its row expression" as a bare requirement.

Minor N36. No method for 'collected and executed' evidence; lane can skip tests

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). Partly right. The omission holds: design.txt:358 says "Record the required suite's collected and executed cases", :411 "Confirm collection and execution of each changed behavior case", :423 "new tests cannot be committed without required-suite execution evidence", :452 "Required tests collect and execute the new behavior coverage", but no line of design.txt names an evidence artifact (grep for log/reuse/rerun/attempt/passage/green finds only unrelated hits at 225, 285, 295, 381). The CI mechanism the finding cites is verbatim: AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:22-24 ("verify that a required CI suite collects and executes it; local execution and the test file's presence are not sufficient"); .github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:538 RUN_TESTS: ${{ needs.tron-build.outputs.tests_required == 'true' || github.run_attempt > 1 }}, every test step 543-590 guarded by if: env.RUN_TESTS == 'true' while the checkout at 540 is unguarded, so the job reports success with all test steps skipped; README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:586-588 and :154-155 ("A rerun executes tests even when the same runtime already passed"). Round 1 never raised this (no hits for passage/run_attempt/RUN_TESTS/Result Reuse in prior-review.txt, r1-findings.md, facts-r1.md), so the revised design has not dispositioned it. What does NOT hold is the risk sentence "records a false claim": bin/ci/tron-build/prepare_handoff.py@2880c3aa9b:41-45,56 sets tests_required false only when has_passed finds a marker keyed by the exact source hash (hash over every tracked blob, gcp-nix.yml:489) and the exact build+environment closure (bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py@2880c3aa9b:30-51); that marker is written only by mark-passed in the Test job (gcp-nix.yml:675-686), which runs only when tests_required was true and after bin/ci/tron-build/require_results.py:10-20 confirmed test-host and test-fpga both succeeded. So a reused-marker green Test host means the identical test binary already executed and passed in an earlier run; the statement "collected and executed" stays true, only the cited run's log would show no execution. Also, every parent commit touching h/ or t/ changes both the source hash and the build closure, so attempt 1 on each new head executes the tests; reuse arises only for an identical tree (re-triggered workflow, merge-queue run with the same tree). The finding's recommendation detail "showing Slice executing ... with the new case names" is unverified (I did not check whether tron-test-host prints Catch2 case names).

Reduced recommendation: add one sentence to step 7 or the CI paragraph naming the artifact, for example "Evidence is the GCP Nix Test host job log of a run whose test steps ran (RUN_TESTS true: first attempt on a new tree, or a GitHub rerun); a run that reused a passage marker (README.ci.md 'Result Reuse') shows skipped steps, so cite the earlier run that executed the identical closure. Record the run URL and attempt number." Note that the parent's own code commits always change the identity, so attempt 1 on each new head executes.
  • design-text lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). Checked every piece of evidence in the finding against the primary sources; all of it holds, and the revised design does not cover the point anywhere. Record the required suite's collected and executed cases."; line 423 "new tests cannot be committed without required-suite execution evidence or the user's explicit exception."; line 452 "Required tests collect and execute the new behavior coverage." So the omission is real, the warning is correct, and the recommendation (name the Test host job log of a run whose steps ran, record run URL and attempt) is consistent with the repository's own documentation.
