    Correction: One precision to add to the finding, not a refutation. The passage marker is keyed by three things, not only the test-runtime identity: a source key (first 7 hex characters of sha256 over git ls-files -s, the tracked-file index, excluding compile_commands.json) [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:486-489], plus the test-runtime and test-environment store paths [test_runtime.py@2880c3aa9b:30-36, 45-51: root / source_key / f"nix-tests-{identity}.passed"]. Any change to a tracked file therefore produces a new marker path, so the first CI attempt after a real code or test change executes the tests. Reuse happens when an identical tracked tree is run again within the three-day marker lifetime [README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:509]: a commit-message-only amend, a rebase that changes no file content, or a re-push of the same tree. The finding's recommendation should say this, and should add the visible sign of reuse: in the "Test host" job every step after checkout shows as skipped, and the final "Test" job runs the step "Verify cached test identity" instead of "Mark exact test identity passed" [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:675-698].
  • intent lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). The finding's evidence holds and its core claim stands; one nuance narrows the failure scenario. Design text checked. The revised design makes execution evidence a deliverable in three places without saying what form it takes or where it comes from: "Record the required suite's collected and executed cases" [design.txt:358], "Confirm collection and execution of each changed behavior case" [design.txt:411], "new tests cannot be committed without required-suite execution evidence" [design.txt:423], "Required tests collect and execute the new behavior coverage" [design.txt:452]. A grep of design.txt for "log", "logs", "attempt", "reuse", "marker" and "rerun" finds no hit. The design does point the implementer at the run-tron-tests skill [design.txt:429]; that skill names the LOCAL Slice log directory ("Slice logs are under logs-$(hostname)/latest/" [.agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b, last paragraph]) but says nothing about CI execution evidence or result reuse. So "names no place to look" is slightly overstated for local runs and exactly right for the CI side. Repository rule checked. AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:22-24 reads verbatim: "Every committed test must run in CI. Before committing it, verify that a required CI suite collects and executes it; local execution and the test file's presence are not sufficient." CI mechanism checked. .github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:538 sets RUN_TESTS: ${{ needs.tron-build.outputs.tests_required == 'true' || github.run_attempt > 1 }}; every test step of the Test host job carries if: env.RUN_TESTS == 'true' (541-590), while the checkout and cleanup steps run unconditionally, so the job reports success with all test steps skipped. The Test job then runs "Mark exact test identity passed" (676-684) or "Verify cached test identity" (688-696) through bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py. README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:586-588: "The first workflow attempt may reuse that marker; a GitHub rerun always executes the host and FPGA tests." Also :154-155 and :644-646 ("Rerunning a host or FPGA test job executes its tests even when ... its original handoff reused an exact passage marker"). Nuance the finding omits (see correction). The passage marker is keyed by the source hash as well as the runtime identity: passed_sentinel returns root / source_key / f"nix-tests-{identity}.passed" [test_runtime.py@2880c3aa9b:45-51], source_hash = sha256 of git ls-files -s over the whole tracked tree [gcp-nix.yml:489], identity = sha256 of the test-runtime and test-environment store paths [test_runtime.py:30-36], tests_required = run_attempt > 1 or not already_passed [test_runtime.py:70-74]. Therefore the first attempt of any push whose tracked tree has not already passed always executes the tests. Reuse can only occur for a merge_group run (trigger at gcp-nix.yml:15) whose merged tree equals an already-passed PR tree, or for a re-push of an identical tree. The false-claim scenario is real but narrower than "the lane can skip tests" suggests. Intent lens. The finding does not move the design away from Ben's request (typed tensor access, comments #2/#3) or jhan's request ("Another agent will implement the design by reading this file", codex-add-tensor-type.md); it adds a process detail that AGENTS.md already mandates and that has no effect on Ben's acceptance. Round-1 F16/C08 asked for the AMX coverage gap to get an owner and a reference to issue #3997 (r1-findings.md:95-110, 164-172) and did not ask for an evidence method, so this is a new round-2 omission, which is allowed. Because the design's Definition of done names the evidence as a deliverable without a form, an implementing agent would have to guess; that is kind (c)/(d) with low consequence, so minor is the right severity.
    Correction: Omission and ambiguity: the design requires the implementer to record that the required suite collected and executed the new cases [design.txt:358, 411, 423, 452] and AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:22-24 makes that verification mandatory before committing, but the design names no CI-side source for that evidence and does not warn that the required GCP Nix "Test host" job reports success with every test step skipped when the exact source hash plus test-runtime identity already has an NFS passage marker [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:538, 541-590, 676-696; test_runtime.py@2880c3aa9b:45-51, 70-74; README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:586-588]. The run-tron-tests skill the design cites [design.txt:429] gives only the local Slice log location. Because the marker key includes the source hash of the whole tracked tree [gcp-nix.yml:489], the first attempt of any newly pushed commit executes the tests; the skip applies to a merge-queue run of an unchanged tree or a re-push of an identical tree. The recommendation stands: name the Test host job log of a run whose test steps ran (RUN_TESTS true) as the evidence, record run URL and attempt number, and state that a green Test host with skipped steps is not execution evidence.

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). Every cited source line says what the finding says. CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:38 is option(BUILD_NATIVE "Probe this host before enabling AVX512" ON). Lines 95-117 run lscpu, check six features (avx512f avx512dq avx512bw avx512vl avx512vbmi2 avx512vpopcntdq), and on any miss run set(AVX512 OFF) and message(WARNING "Disabling AVX512: ${FEATURE} not supported"); the normal-variable set shadows the -DAVX512=ON cache entry for if(AVX512) in src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:269-272 (defines TRON_AVX512_ENABLED), and h/tron/simd/auto.hpp@2880c3aa9b:17-21 makes TRON_CHUNK_SIZE 8 without that define. CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:30-39 (preset native) sets only CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE and inherits base-ninja, which does not set BUILD_NATIVE; lines 40-48 define preset cross-avx512 with BUILD_NATIVE OFF and AVX512 ON, "Cross-compile for AVX-512 from a non-AVX-512 host"; GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:987-995 (Note [Cross-Compile for AVX-512]) says the same. Nix CI itself passes -DBUILD_NATIVE=OFF -DAVX512=ON (nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix@2880c3aa9b:86,88), so the repository's own CI avoids the probe. The revised design uses cmake --preset native -DAVX512=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=OFF/ON (design.txt:411-412) and names sw-dev-01 as the build host (design.txt:430); grep of design.txt for BUILD_NATIVE, cross-avx512, "Disabling AVX", lscpu, or an AVX-512 host statement returns nothing, so the omission is real. Round-1 F47 (r1-findings.md) asked only for the 8-lane flags and the baseline check; the revised row 3 (design.txt:413) covers that, but neither F47 nor the revision addressed the probe. Two facts limit the severity. First, the AMX-on row fails loudly via the #error at self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b:30-36 (round-1 F47's verifier correction already cited this guard at f46e48ba), so only the AMX-off row is silent. Second, the prescribed host very likely passes the probe: the memory note claude-box-tron-build-env.md records sw-dev-01 as an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, and this container (hostname claude-agentsrv, same CPU model; codex's ~/.codex/AGENTS.md:27-28 places claude-box on sw-dev-01) lists all six required flags in /proc/cpuinfo (avx512f avx512dq avx512bw avx512vl avx512_vbmi2 avx512_vpopcntdq; the probe normalizes the underscore spellings at CMakeLists.txt:106-107). I cannot confirm from source that this container is sw-dev-01, so that point is medium confidence. One extra point supports the recommendation: the design also tells the implementer to run make build-test and make test-host (design.txt:431), and those targets reconfigure with cmake --preset $(CMAKE_PRESET) ... (GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:532, 541, 553) where CMAKE_PRESET is native only if /proc/cpuinfo has avx512f and cross-avx512 otherwise (GNUmakefile:226-237), so on a non-AVX-512 host the design's two build routes would configure differently. Severity stays minor: on the named host nothing degrades, and on another host the mislabeled AMX-off run is the only silent failure, fixable by one sentence.
    Correction: The omission holds, but the mechanism sentence over-reaches. Only the "16-lane, AMX code off" row (design.txt:411) can silently become an 8-lane build. The "16-lane, AMX code on" row (design.txt:412) cannot degrade silently: the TRON_AMX_DISPATCH definition does not depend on AVX512 (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:219-224, 329-332), and h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b:30-36 has #if defined(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH) && TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16 followed by #error "TRON_AMX_DISPATCH requires TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 ...", so that row fails at compile time on a host where the probe turns AVX512 off. Corrected claim: "Omission: the 16-lane rows pass -DAVX512=ON to preset native, which keeps BUILD_NATIVE on; CMake probes lscpu and sets AVX512 OFF with only a configure-log warning when a required feature is missing. The design names sw-dev-01 as the build host without stating that it has AVX-512, and does not name the cross-avx512 preset (BUILD_NATIVE OFF, AVX512 ON) that exists for this case." Recommendation as written, plus: say that the AMX-on row fails loudly, so the log check matters for the AMX-off row.

The current agent host (claude-agentsrv, same container lineage per notebook artifacts/dev-machines/README.md:4) is an AMD Ryzen whose lscpu passes all six probed features (checked locally with the probe's own normalization). On that host the probe does not disable AVX512, so the scenario does not occur. - The design also says "Run the relevant existing targets through the repository's documented build commands" (design.txt:407) and names make build-test / make test-host (design.txt:431). GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:226-231 picks cross-avx512 automatically when /proc/cpuinfo lacks avx512f and prints "Cross-compiling for AVX-512: executable will not run on this machine". The make path is already protected; only the literal cmake --preset native commands in the table bypass it. - No effect on Ben's acceptance (Ben's comments #2/#3 are about typed tensor access, not the build recipe) and none on jhan's request. Net: a one-sentence hardening ("check the configure log for 'Disabling AVX512'; on a host without AVX-512 use preset cross-avx512, whose binaries run only on an AVX-512 host") is correct and cheap, but no change is required for the design to be implementable on the host it names. Severity by consequence: note.
    Correction: Omission, low consequence: the table's cmake --preset native -DAVX512=ON rows (design.txt:411-412) leave the BUILD_NATIVE lscpu probe on (CMakeLists.txt:38, 95-117@2880c3aa9b). On a host without the six probed AVX-512 features the probe sets AVX512 OFF with only a warning. Optional one-sentence addition under Build configurations: confirm the configure log has no "Disabling AVX512" warning; on a host without AVX-512 use --preset cross-avx512 (BUILD_NATIVE OFF, AVX512 ON), whose binaries run only on an AVX-512 host.

Minor N40. objdump procedure lacks symbols, build type, fp16 baseline

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). Checked against primary sources at live main 2880c3aa9b and the revised design text. (1) Preset: CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:37 sets "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE": "RelWithDebInfo" for preset native; CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b overrides only the Debug flags (:80 CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG_INIT), so RelWithDebInfo keeps CMake's default -O2 -g. The finding's fact holds. (2) fp16 in the test: git show 2880c3aa9b:t/t_llama_unit.cpp | grep -n fp16 returns only line 1081, a scale constant. Every direct set_v call in that file passes float or bf16: 142 (float array filled at 139), 796 and 1554 (std::array<bf16>), 1723, 1923, 2533-2535, 2568-2569, 2690, 2705, 2721, 2792, 2802 (float buffers or bf16 tensors). The finding's claim holds and covers more callers than it lists. (3) Indirect fp16 instantiation: the only library-side set_v caller is save_v_impl [h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2831], whose source pointer element is the executor's btensor_t element; that element is fp16 only for host_fp16 = make_llm_executor<false, tensor, hardware::htensor, tensor> [common.hpp:102; amx_attn_iface.hpp:155-156 "host stores float and host_fp16 stores fp16"]. t_llama_unit instantiates only make_llm_executor<false, tensor, tensor, tensor> models (t_llama_unit.cpp:1252, 1298, 1323, 1852, 1986) plus tp1 aliases (bf16 btensor) for static checks (1223-1228). git grep host_fp16|htensor at 2880c3aa9b hits no src/ file and no t_llama_unit line. So the baseline t_llama_unit binary carries no fp16 set_v body (inferred from instantiation analysis; no build was run). (4) Design text: design.txt:440 asks to "Inspect the caller bodies containing bf16/fp16/float even and odd V appends" in "both built t_llama_unit binaries", and design.txt:415 fixes the baseline as the unmodified recorded main commit, while the fp16 source rows are added only by the head-build test row (design.txt:396). The internal inconsistency the finding names is real. (5) Symbols: design.txt:440-441 names no symbol or caller function; it describes regions functionally. Literally true. Two corrections to the finding: (a) the optimization level is implicitly fixed, because design.txt:422 names cmake --preset native and design.txt:439 says "same pinned compiler, preset, optimization flags"; an agent following the named preset cannot pick a different level, so this part is an explicit-statement omission, not an ambiguity. (b) The recommendation to "locate ... set_v<, append_v<, scaled_v_expr" as symbols conflicts with the code: set_v, append_v and scaled_v_expr members are TRON(inline) = inline __attribute__((always_inline)) [h/common/attributes.hpp@2880c3aa9b:78; kv_cache.hpp:1645-1660, 2288-2289], and test targets get INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION when LTO is supported [CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:82-83, 157], so they will not appear as standalone symbols; the design's "caller bodies" framing (design.txt:440) is the correct unit. Only book::allocate_kv_group [kv_cache.hpp:1199, no inline attribute] and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage [kv_cache.hpp:963, TRON(nodiscard) only] may survive as standalone symbols, and even those may be inlined under LTO.
    Correction: Ambiguity and omission (minor): the instruction-comparison procedure (design.txt:439-441) describes the regions to inspect functionally but names no caller function or symbol, and it asks to inspect fp16 V appends in both t_llama_unit binaries although the baseline binary at the recorded main commit contains no fp16 set_v body (t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b has no fp16 set_v call, and no linked source instantiates the host_fp16 executor); the fp16 rows exist only in the head build (design.txt:396). Drop the "optimization level" part: the design names cmake --preset native (design.txt:422) and "same ... preset, optimization flags" (design.txt:439), and that preset pins CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE RelWithDebInfo (CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:37), so the level is determined; stating "RelWithDebInfo (-O2 -g)" explicitly is optional. Fix the recommendation: do not list set_v<, append_v< or scaled_v_expr as symbols to locate, because they are always_inline (attributes.hpp:78) and the build uses LTO (CMakeLists.txt:157); instead say "locate the t_llama_unit test bodies that call set_v/append_v/scaled_v (identify them from the source), and book::allocate_kv_group / restore_reclaimable_kv_storage if they survive as standalone symbols", and add "the baseline t_llama_unit has no fp16 set_v instantiation; compare fp16 in a binary that instantiates the host_fp16 executor, or record that fp16 has no baseline in this comparison."

Step 2 warns "These helpers are often forced inline; absence of a standalone helper symbol is not a passed comparison" [design.txt:440]. So N40's recommendation to "locate ... set_v<, append_v<, scaled_v_expr" in the demangled output asks for symbols that always_inline removes, contradicting the design's correct guidance. Round-1 F17's verifier corrections asked exactly for the tool, the configuration mapping, and the inlining warning [r1-findings.md, F17 verifier corrections]; the revised design supplied all three [design.txt:411-413, 439-441]. (3) "the baseline t_llama_unit contains no fp16 set_v call" -- HOLDS, verified. Every set_v call in t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b resolves to the float or bf16 overload: line 142 passes std::array<float> (decl 135); 796 and 1554 pass std::array<bf16> (decls 794, 1552); 1723 passes btensor rows (decl 1711; btensor = dmatensor<bf16> at h/tron/hardware/btensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:21); 1923, 2705, 2792 pass float buffers (decls 1919, 2701, 2788); 2533, 2535, 2568, 2569, 2690, 2721, 2802 pass tensor<head_size>::data, which is std::array<float, N> [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:31-34]. The save_v path at 1929/1933 uses make_llm_executor<false, tensor, tensor, tensor> [t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:1851-1852], so save_v_impl [h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2831] instantiates the float overload there. The only fp16 mention in the file is a scale constant [line 1081]. The head test row adds "Exercise bf16, fp16, and float source rows" [design.txt:395], so the fp16 body exists only in the head binary, and step 2's "both built t_llama_unit binaries" cannot be satisfied for fp16. N40's alternative "compare fp16 in a model binary that saves fp16 activations" is weak: the fp16 executor host_fp16 [h/tron/models/common.hpp@2880c3aa9b:102] is referenced only by t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp and t_amx_numerics.cpp, and t_amx_dispatch_dtype's set_v call passes std::array<bf16> [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:95-98]; no production model target uses host_fp16 (git grep host_fp16 at 2880c3aa9b over h, src, t, ingest). The actionable fix is the "record that fp16 has no baseline" clause. Severity: minor. The implementing agent notices the missing fp16 baseline body immediately and cannot build the wrong thing from it; a one-sentence addition to step 2 resolves it. The other two parts would not change any action the agent takes.
    Correction: Omission (minor): step 2 of the instruction comparison asks to inspect "bf16/fp16/float even and odd V appends" in BOTH t_llama_unit binaries [design.txt:440], but the baseline t_llama_unit instantiates no fp16 page::set_v; every baseline set_v call passes float or bf16, and the fp16 source-row coverage is added only by the head test row [design.txt:395]. The design should say that the fp16 append comparison is head-only in t_llama_unit (record "no baseline body") or name a different binary. Drop the other two parts of N40: the optimization level is already fixed because the design names cmake --preset native and the preset sets CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo, and the function names are already given in sections 5-7 while the design's "forced inline, no standalone symbol" warning is correct, so N40's recipe to locate set_v< / append_v< symbols would misdirect the agent.

Minor N43. F25 vocabulary fix not applied though listed as accepted

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). I re-derived every part of the finding from the primary sources. The finding holds, with two nuances (see correction). Disposition row confirmed. design.txt:469 reads "F14 F15 F25 F29 F45 C04 C05 C07 | Accepted as future child work | Specify stacked base, topical reconstruction, accessor changes, lane-sized K stores, typed-owner tests, generator file, and scratch lifetime." So codex records F25 as accepted. F25's three narrowed items (r1-findings.md, F25 "Still missing" list, items 1-3): Item (2) is applied. design.txt:378 names "store_row/load_row, moving scatter_row/gather_row address calculations into the K type's operations" and :379 "page::set_k_block ... Call typed store_block(view, block, mask, rows)". The phrase "block write" no longer appears anywhere in design.txt (grep returned nothing). The finding agrees this item is done. Item (3) is NOT applied. design.txt:107 reads "Threads share the K-store work." and :109 reads "It does not change how threads divide the K-store work." The phrase "shared block save" appears nowhere in design.txt except inside the code Note name "Note [Shared block save]" at :383. The PR title is "VNNI K: store the K cache of 128-dimension heads in the AMX VNNI layout, with a shared block save" (github-review.json .pr.title). jhan's rule (memory vnni-k-terminology, 2026-09-15): "save" = the operation, "store" = the CPU instruction; use "shared block save" in any new page about this branch. Item (1) is NOT applied. The Words row at design.txt:22 (and the HTML <tr> for "VNNI, native K, packed V, blocked packed K") says only "PR #4424's blocked packed K groups dimension pairs within token blocks", with no link and no code name. The strings "VNNI layout", "pair-interleaved" and "VNNI K layout" occur nowhere in design-new-tensor-type.html (regex search over the whole file returned no match). The code calls the layout the "VNNI pair-interleaved layout" (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:656, inside Note [K VNNI storage] which starts at :653) and "the VNNI K layout" (h/tron/models/model.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:2735). So the term bridge F25 asked for is still missing. Line 383 confirmed verbatim: "K stores differ from V stores. A K token owns separate 4-byte lanes in a shared cache line. Its row store may use a lane scatter or a lane-masked store ... Several workers can write different token lanes of that line during Note [Shared block save]." Here "row store" names the operation and "lane-masked store" the instruction, so the sentence mixes the two senses jhan's rule separates. The technical content matches the code: model.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:2763-2765 "Their writers use masked stores on disjoint token lanes. So two threads may write one block without conflict." and :2742 "Block save (k_vnni::store_block, page::set_k_block)". Verification of the finding's citations: the file is h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp (the finding wrote bare "kv_cache.hpp"); Note [K VNNI storage] spans :653-708 at 30c4ac82cbb6 (the finding said 653-705; trivial). model.hpp line numbers 2742 and 2763-2765 are exact.
    Correction: Two nuances narrow the finding without overturning it. (a) Item (1) is partly mitigated: the design does name Note [K VNNI storage] once, at design.txt:383 (plain <code>, no link), so an implementer who reads section 7 reaches the child's Note by indirection; what is still missing is the one-sentence bridge in the Words row saying that "blocked packed K" is the code's "VNNI (pair-interleaved) K layout", and the layout's code name appears nowhere in the design. (b) The line-383 "store" wording is a deviation from jhan's prose rule, not a contradiction of the code: the child's own Note uses "store" as the operation noun ("save_k ... stores K with page::set_k_block", "That store scatters", kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:673-685), the PR body says "The K store of this branch", and the design's typed operations are named store_row/store_block after Ben's sketch (design.txt:378-379). Note N07. Reviewer questions do not say which sections change on a No

2 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). I re-derived the finding from the primary sources and it holds. (1) The omission is real. The reviewer-question table has exactly two columns, "Question" and "Proposed answer" [design.txt:80-85]. A grep of the whole design text for "No", "otherwise", "alternative", "fall back" and "sketch" finds no sentence that maps a No answer to the sections that would change; the only alternative named is indirect ("In the sketch, the layout is a template argument of both the owner and the view", design.txt:59; "It avoids a public layout-policy template", design.txt:62). The design does gate implementation on the answers: section 8's acceptance list says "The reviewer questions have recorded answers, and the implemented interface matches them" [design.txt:449], and section 9 marks F02/F03/F04/F26/F51/F52 as "Accepted; reviewer answers pending" [design.txt:464]. So an implementer who receives a No has no guidance, which is what the finding says. Round-1 F02 asked codex to list the questions and mark the design conditional [r1-findings.md:20]; it did not ask for the consequence of a No, so N07 is a new round-2 point, not a re-raise of an addressed one. (2) The four per-question consequences check out against the sources. Q1: the sketch's alternative is vnni_view<T, Layout> / vnni_tensor<Layout> with the address formula in a layout struct (Ben comment 5765866077, github-review.json; facts-r1.md:29), which would replace the per-layout declarations at design.txt:198-205. Note N49. chunk_size column rule: keep, gap unobservable

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity note). Every part of the finding holds against primary sources at live main 2880c3aa9b (kv_cache.hpp lives at h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp; the file is unchanged since c7844ca2ce, so line numbers match). (1) The type rule is looser than set_v's rule. design.txt:180 says "Its column count must be positive and divisible by chunk_size, the selected SIMD width" and design.txt:271 says "Type constraints are positive even rows and positive columns divisible by chunk_size; keep stricter constraints on individual operations" (both quotes verbatim). chunk_size is 16 in the AVX-512 build and 8 otherwise [h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17-21@2880c3aa9b]. set_v requires head_size % 32 == 0 [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1622-1623, 1645-1648@2880c3aa9b]. The book-level storage check is head_size % chunk_size != 0 -> false [kv_cache.hpp:587], so the type rule equals the existing book rule, and 16 < 32 makes the gap real on paper. (2) No test geometry sits in the gap. Every kv_geometry literal in t/ at 2880c3aa9b is 64, 128 or 256, plus the deliberately invalid {1, 65} [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:191, 230, 437, 480-482, 836-838, 1112-1116, 1254, 1390; t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:62-64]; the wide scaled_v test uses 256 and 512 [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:1200-1205]; every head_size = N constant in t/ is 64 or 128 (t_fp32, t_hwattention*, t_amx_dispatch_dtype:64, t_llama_unit, t_rope_integrity). The only other head_dim in t/data is the gemma4 vision_config head_dim: 72 [t/data/config-gemma4-31b-wrapper.json:218], which is a vision tower, not a KV-cache geometry, and 72 is not divisible by 16 anyway. (3) No production geometry can sit in the gap, and the reason is stronger than the finding's evidence. llama.hpp:147 is size_t head_size = 128;, a DEFAULT member of llm_configuration, not a fixed production value; ingest-generated models emit tron::kv_geometry{kv_heads, head_size} from the model's head_dim [ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:353, 574, 639@2880c3aa9b], and the repo does not store head_dim for the 23 CI-primed models [bin/ci/prime_hf_models.py]. What closes the gap is compile-time enforcement: the single production V-save site calls pg.template set_v<geometry.kv>(...) unconditionally under #if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 [h/tron/models/model.hpp:2830-2832], and the software-attention path calls page.template scaled_v<geometry.kv>(...) unconditionally [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1842, 1846]; scaled_v_expr's constructor requires head_size in {64, 128, 256, 512} [kv_cache.hpp:2070-2071]; mock.hpp:87-88 documents the same. So a model with head size 80 or 48 does not compile on main today in the 16-lane build; the design's looser type rule cannot make such a geometry reachable. The gap is therefore unobservable by construction, as the finding says. (4) Build dependence and 8-lane use. In the 8-lane build kv_block stores V row-major [kv_cache.hpp:2195-2202] and model.hpp:2833-2836 writes V through .v<geometry.kv>(...).set(...), so the packed type has no production use there, matching design.txt:271 "Keep row-major V in the 8-lane cache; the packed type still must be complete for the unconditionally compiled AMX test substitutes." The finding's cited lines (llama.hpp:147, mock.hpp:91, t_llama_unit.cpp:191/230/437/836-838/1112-1116/1199-1205, heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:62-64, kv_cache.hpp:1623, design lines 180 and 271) all say what the finding says. Only imprecision: llama.hpp:147 is a default, not proof for ingest-generated production models; the compile-time requires clauses are the proof. That does not change the verdict (keep, no change required).

The design already makes and justifies that choice at line 225 ("A stride-2 ordinary row view has the right addresses but uses scalar extraction; it is not the bulk-read implementation"). (3) "Expression precedent the reviewer asked for": Ben's review 5270587330 (github-review.json) says "follow the precedent already present in tron: we currently have types like tensor and dtensor which provide a uniform interface based upon expr". Confirmed. (4) "No production code at main reads V through an expression": V readers outside kv_cache.hpp at 2880c3aa9b are self_attention.hpp:1681 (v_data), :1842 and :1846 (scaled_v), full.hpp:2654 (get_v); nothing constructs a tensor from a V plane or reads a V row through a rank-1 expr. The design keeps that expression and says its address lookup happens "only inside the typed implementation" (design.txt line 316), so it does not go through row.chunk(). The finding's conclusion (the row's chunk()/bf16_chunk() have only the section 8 test as consumer) stands. One iteration is exactly chunk(i) / bf16_chunk(i). The design at line 225 already names the same two instructions but sources them from scaled_v_expr's even_part/odd_part and says "narrow the selected halves for bf16 reads" without naming get_v(bf16*), which already has the narrowing. Section 9 rows for F08/F34/F37 and F11/F31/F32/F35/F47 (lines 466-467) record the related dispositions. The finding recommends no change, so there is nothing to refute; its facts are right.

Source facts. h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp is unchanged between f46e48bab498 and 2880c3aa9b (empty git diff). Its generic overload operator()(expr<B, in_d0, in_d1> const& v_in, size_t offset0, Offsets...) at slice.hpp:147-177 is constrained only by requires(d0 != DYN_SIZE && sizeof...(ds) == 1) (line 148) and captures the input by reference: lines 168-169 read "// It's critical that v_in be captured by reference here." / "auto f = [=, &v_in](size_t i) {". The design's packed view inherits the rank-2 expr base (design.txt:211 "v_vnni_view<T,R,D> inherits expr<view_type,R,D>") and does not inherit views<> (design.txt:213), so it matches neither the by-value view/const_view overloads (slice.hpp:53, 90) nor the const_views overload (slice.hpp:125), and it does match the generic expr overload by derived-to-base deduction. The returned lambda calls v_in[i + offset0] (slice.hpp:170), which the rank-2 expr base forwards to self()[i] (h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:57-65 @2880c3aa9b, file unchanged since f46e48bab498), and wraps the row in slice_expr<row&&, d1> (slice.hpp:174). slice_expr (expr.hpp:693-732) requires the row to satisfy the expression concept (expr.hpp:140-143: derives from expr<Self, Self::size_>), which design.txt:211 "v_vnni_row<T,D> inherits expr<row_type,D>" satisfies; it stores the row by value (sub_expr, expr.hpp:145-147) and forwards only chunk/bf16_chunk/fp16_chunk; the packed row provides chunk and bf16_chunk (design.txt:220-221) and the rank-1 expr base supplies fp16_chunk by conversion (expr.hpp:119-126). So an lvalue packed view can be sliced with zero edits, and the result holds a reference to that view. Design text. design.txt:277 says "No packed slices or iterators ... Leave h/tron/tensor/slice.hpp unchanged ... This scope decision removes the unneeded odd-boundary slice-write and temporary-slice lifetime questions." Every other slice mention (design.txt:30, 33, 63, 85, 352, 429, 432, 466, 504) is a definition, a scope statement or a bin/slice command; none says the existing generic expression slice already accepts a packed view, and none names the leave-as-is versus one-deleted-overload choice that the round-1 F08 verifier corrections asked for (r1-findings.md, F08 verifier correction (b): "either leave the generic expr path as is or add one constraint, and name the choice", with suggested text "The existing generic expression slice [slice.hpp:147-177] already accepts an lvalue packed view through its rank-2 expr base; do not pass a temporary to it."). The verification table at design.txt:393-401 has no slice-lifetime row. So the residual the finding names is real: the revised text closes F08's speculative-code part but drops the verifier's explicit ask to name the existing path. Two refinements, neither refuting. (1) The finding cites "expr.hpp:695-732" without a directory; the file is h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp, not h/tron/tensor/. (2) The recommendation understates the Owner& hazard. Inside the Owner& overload (slice.hpp:38-42) owner is a named lvalue, so owner.as_view() selects the lvalue-qualified as_view() (the deleted rvalue forms at design.txt:210 do not fire), and the resulting prvalue view can bind only to the generic expr overload (a non-const prvalue cannot bind Owner&; it is not a view/const_view/const_views specialization). That overload captures the temporary view by reference, and the temporary dies at the end of the return statement in slice.hpp:41. So passing ANY packed owner, lvalue or temporary, through slice<>(owner, ...) yields a dangling reference, whereas an ordinary tensor owner is safe today because its as_view() returns a view<> that the by-value overload at slice.hpp:53 copies. The added sentence should say "do not pass the owner itself" rather than "a temporary owner".

Note N57. Test paragraph omits poison-fill path and index() location

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity note). Both ambiguity claims hold against the primary sources. (1) Poison fill: the revised paragraph reads, verbatim, "Adapt t_k_vnni_layout to create actual aligned k_vnni_tensor owners and call typed store/load/block/reader operations through as_view(). Retain the independent index expectations. For physical-byte checks, copy the trivially copyable owner's object representation into a test buffer. Do not use detail::vnni_access to recreate raw production calls." [design.txt:385]. It names the copy-OUT direction only. The current test writes poison INTO the plane directly at t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:107-109 (for (auto& x : buf->plane) x = tron::bf16::from_bits(POISON_0XA5A5);), :190-192 (same on ref->plane, then memcpy to blk->plane at :193) and :286-288 (NAN_POISON_0X7FC1). Under the design, packed views have "No public pointer constructor, .data member, or pointer conversion" [design.txt:221] and detail::vnni_access is "used only by tensor operations and layout-specific kernels" [design.txt:223], so the direct fill is gone and no replacement is named. The two legitimate routes exist (64 typed store_row calls cover every slot because "Token i owns column (i % 16) of token block (i / 16) in every panel" [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:28-29] and 64 x 128 = 8192 elements = the whole 16 KiB plane [k_vnni.hpp:22]; or memcpy into the trivially copyable owner), but the implementer must pick one unaided. (2) index location: the anchors are using tron::k_vnni::index; STATIC_REQUIRE(index(0, 0) == 0); ... [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp@30c4ac82cbb6:80-90] and index is constexpr size_t index(size_t token, size_t dim) noexcept in namespace tron::k_vnni [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:42, 101-107]. The design says only "Retain the independent index expectations" [design.txt:385], "This header contains the K mapping and storage operations" [design.txt:369] and "Port the K mapping and vector routines" [design.txt:368]; it names k_vnni::layout_on by namespace [design.txt:370] but never names index, its home, or whether it becomes a static member of k_vnni_view. Round-1 C07's verifier corrections raised exactly this point (index may become "a static mapping member of k_vnni_view; the STATIC_REQUIRE anchor cases then need renaming"; "whether index() remains a public constexpr function") [r1-findings.md, C07 entry], and the revision's disposition row "Accepted as future child work ... typed-owner tests" [design.txt:469] did not answer it. One premise in the finding is imprecise (see correction), but it does not carry either claim. Severity note is right: both gaps are one-clause additions, either resolution compiles and the expected values are unchanged.
    Correction: Premise clause only: "copying the trivially copyable owner's object representation out is sound when sizeof(k_vnni_tensor<64,128>) is 16384 bytes, which the block-size rule requires" over-extends design.txt:328. That rule ("Require ... the existing block byte size") is stated in section 6 for the parent's V owner and kv_block, not for the child's K owner; the design nowhere states a byte-size rule for k_vnni_tensor. Also, memcpy-out is well-defined for any trivially copyable type regardless of size; the 16384-byte size matters only for the memcmp against the 16 KiB reference plane (k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:22 "64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB"). Corrected premise: "copying the trivially copyable owner's bytes out is sound; comparing them to a 16 KiB reference plane additionally assumes sizeof(k_vnni_tensor<64,128>) == 16384, which the design does not state for the K owner." The two ambiguity claims and the recommendation stand unchanged.

Note N60. cmake preset flags vs make targets: cache caveats unstated

3 of 3 verifiers could not refute it

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity note). The finding holds in substance. I re-derived each claim from the primary sources at live main 2880c3aa9b and from the revised design text. What the design says. Line 407 says "Run the relevant existing targets through the repository's documented build commands." Lines 411-413 give three cmake --preset native -DAVX512=... -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=... configurations. Line 430 names make build-test and make test-host as the required checks. A grep of design.txt for gen/, CMakeCache, reconfigure, worktree, cross-avx512 and BUILD_NATIVE returns only lines 407-413 and 439, so the cache interplay is not stated anywhere. Section 9 line 467 records F47 as "explicit build flags", so the revision added the cmake lines but nothing about how the Make targets treat them. The run-tron-tests skill at 2880c3aa9b, which line 428 tells the implementer to read, mentions gen/ only at its line 75 (do not replace public wrappers with gen/ binaries) and has no cache caveat either. So the omission is real and not already handled. Make reconfigures gen/ with its own preset and flag list. GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:351-353 build-test: gen/config/test then cmake --build gen. :538-543 gen/config/test: does rm -rf gen/config then cmake --preset $(CMAKE_PRESET) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=... -DBUILD_TEST_MODELS=ON -DBUILD_INGEST_MODELS=ON .... A grep of the whole GNUmakefile for AVX512 finds only HAS_AVX512 (:227-228) and comments (:993-995); TRON_AMX never appears. rm -rf gen/config removes only the stamp directory (created by mkdir -p gen/config; touch gen/config/test at :544-545), not gen/CMakeCache.txt, so hand-passed AVX512 and TRON_AMX_DISPATCH values survive only as cache entries. After a hand cmake --preset native -D... the stamp gen/config/test does not exist, so the first make build-test does reconfigure. The native preset's cacheVariables are CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE plus the base-ninja compiler settings (CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:9-39), so they do not touch AVX512 or TRON_AMX_DISPATCH and the cached values persist. The 8-lane branch (:1674-1725) declares only v() and v_ptr(). Definitions sit under "#if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16" at :2281-2532. That macro is added by src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:271 under the AVX512 option (CMakeLists.txt:44 "option(AVX512 ...)"). So -DAVX512=OFF gives the 8-lane branch. - t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:287 is a plain TEST_CASE (not a template). Line 228 "using heterogeneous_model = model<heterogeneous_scheduler_tp1>;" is a concrete type, and model.hpp:746 "using page = cache_t::page_t;" maps it to the kv_cache.hpp page template. Lines 443-444 call "page->set_v<software_geometry.kv>(...)" on that concrete type with no TRON_CHUNK_SIZE guard (the file has no #if at all; its only preprocessor lines are #include at 1-26). TEST_CASE "scaled_v padding NaN" (:2658, non-template, concrete book_t at :2663) calls set_v at :2690, :2705, :2721, :2792, :2802 with no guard. TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE "scaled_v" (:1665) calls p->set_v at :1723 with no guard and is instantiated for both listed cache types. The same lines exist at 98bb8cb22f94 (the design's recorded main tip). So the 8-lane test build fails at baseline for the required suite as well, and writing "16-lane builds only" on the t_heterogeneous_scheduler row alone would wrongly imply that t_llama_unit compiles in the 8-lane build. The note belongs on the 8-lane row (design.txt:413), which already says "Establish the unmodified-baseline result before attributing a failure to the parent", and design.txt:439 already says "Start with the 16-lane AMX-enabled configuration above." Rejected N19. store_row renamed append_v_row: unasked, asymmetric with K family

Candidate claim: Design decision I disagree with, plus ambiguity. The reviewer named the bulk V write store_row. The design renames it append_v_row while keeping the reviewer's load_row for V and, in the child, store_row/load_row/store_block for K, so the same operation carries two verbs across the two families. The rename is stated but is not among the questions for the reviewer. The verb append already names page::append_v (the cross-page token copy), which the design maps to copy_token; after the change, append_v (calls copy_token) and append_v_row (the row store) would mean different things in the same header.

  • source lens: holds (high confidence, severity minor). Core claim holds; two supporting sub-claims are wrong and one is misleading. VERIFIED: design.txt:229 "append_v_row is this design's name for the sketch's V store_row"; design.txt:232-236 give the V family as append_v_row / load_row / copy_token / copy_plane; design.txt:378-379 give the child K family as "typed store_row/load_row" and "typed store_block(view, block, mask, rows)"; the four reviewer questions at design.txt:78-85 (address formula, const view, operator[], scope) do not mention the name, while the const-rule deviation from the sketch IS flagged there ("This differs from the sketch's span-like rule", design.txt:82). Ben's comment 5765866077 section 4 declares store_row/load_row for k_vnni_layout with "// Corresponding overloads for v_vnni_layout." (evidence/github-review.json). So the V bulk write carries a different verb than the sketch and than the child's K family, and that deviation is not among the questions. REFUTED sub-claim 1 ("in the same header"): design.txt:241 puts append_v_row in h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp; page::append_v stays a page member of kv_cache.hpp (design.txt:256 "Keep the name"; kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1873). Different headers. REFUTED sub-claim 2 ("would mean different things"): both operations are fresh-destination cache appends with the identical partner rule; design.txt:229 and :243 state the same even-zeros/odd-preserves contract for append_v_row and copy_token, design.txt:298-300 labels both "Even cache append"/"Odd cache append", and the existing comment at kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1867-1870 says append_v's even path zeros the odd partner because append_v is only called via copy_from in append() on fresh ranges. The verb "append" is thus the existing tron term for this write rule, which is the design's stated rationale. MISLEADING sub-claim 3 ("unasked"): append_v_row was already the ORIGINAL design's name (prior-review.txt: 10 mentions; r1-findings.md:247 lists it among defined names); round-1 F38's verifier correction asked for exactly a mapping "Ben store_row -> append_v_row" (r1-findings.md:368), which design.txt:229 supplies; no retained round-1 finding asked to rename it to store_row (F08 at r1-findings.md:51 used "store_row" only inside a scope list and was dispositioned as scope reduction, design.txt:463-466). Also, the memory rule vnni-k-terminology ("save = the operation; store = the CPU instruction only") argues AGAINST the finding's first alternative (store_row for both families), not for it; the second alternative (keep append_v_row, add a reviewer question) is unaffected.
    Correction: Design decision I disagree with (minor). The V bulk write is named append_v_row while the sketch names it store_row (with "Corresponding overloads for v_vnni_layout"), and the design's own child table keeps the sketch's store_row/load_row/store_block for K (design.txt:378-379); so the two layout families use different verbs for the row write. The design flags its const-rule deviation from the sketch as a reviewer question (design.txt:82) but not this name deviation (design.txt:78-85). Fix: add one question row: "The V bulk write is named append_v_row, not the sketch's store_row, because the name records the cache rule (even write zeros its partner, odd write preserves it) and matches the existing page::append_v; K keeps store_row/load_row/store_block. Acceptable?" Drop the sub-claims that append_v and append_v_row "would mean different things in the same header": they live in different headers (vnni.hpp vs kv_cache.hpp) and share the same fresh-destination partner rule (design.txt:229, :243; kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1867-1870). Drop "unasked": round-1 F38 accepted the name and asked only for the mapping sentence, which design.txt:229 provides.
  • design-text lens: refuted (high confidence, severity note). The finding attacks a naming choice the revised design flags as deliberate, and its evidence does not show the choice is wrong. 1. Deliberate and explained. design.txt:229: "append_v_row is this design's name for the sketch's V store_row. The name records its cache semantics: an even destination zeros its odd partner; an odd destination preserves its even partner." design.txt:11 frames every interface choice as a proposal: "The interface choices below are concrete proposals; the reviewer questions remain open before implementation." The finding concedes "The rename is stated". 2. The asymmetry with K is not "the same operation" under two verbs. The V row write has a partner side effect (zero or preserve the pair partner). The child's K row write has none: design.txt:383 "A K token owns separate 4-byte lanes in a shared cache line. Its row store may use a lane scatter or a lane-masked store; it must never read, merge, and rewrite a whole 64-byte line." The child code confirms this: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:139-147 scatter_row issues 4 dword scatters of one token's lanes and touches no other token. So the design gives V a verb that records its extra semantics and leaves K with Ben's plain store_row; that is the stated rationale at line 229, not an oversight. The design also chose separate V and K families with separate owners (design.txt:62 "one concrete view per layout"; design.txt:82, a listed reviewer question), so no generic code will call one overload set on both layouts; a shared verb buys nothing technically. 3. The "would mean different things" claim is inaccurate and the mapping is explicit. page::append_v (kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1866-1920) and append_v_row share the identical partner rule (even destination zeroes, odd preserves, lines 1877-1919 comments "store [0 b]" / "store [b d]"); both write one token into the packed V plane and differ only in source form (packed page vs contiguous row). The design maps each existing page method to exactly one typed operation: design.txt:252 "page::set_v ... Forward to append_v_row. save_v_impl -> page::set_v -> append_v_row"; design.txt:256 "page::append_v Keep the name; call copy_token."; design.txt:303 "Production packed-V row writes use page::set_v or page::append_v. Both call the typed append/copy operations." An implementing agent has no guess to make. The finding's "in the same header" is also imprecise: append_v_row lives in h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp (design.txt:241, 350) and page::append_v in kv_cache.hpp. 4. The finding's own cited memory rule cuts against its first option. vnni-k-terminology.md (jhan 2026-09-15): "save = the operation ... store = the CPU instruction only". Rejected N26. Array placement-new contradicts linked C09 warning; no-cookie rule unstated

Candidate claim: Ambiguity: the design prescribes the array placement form ::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[block_count];, and that form is correct, but the round-1 page it links under [C09] says the array form 'may consume unspecified extra bytes' and should not be used. The disposition row marks C09 'Accepted' and the design gives no basis for overriding that warning, so an implementing agent reading both documents must guess. The basis is: the void* placement argument selects the library function operator new[](std::size_t, void*), which C++20 and later exempt from array allocation overhead (CWG 2382, [expr.new]/17 in N4950); independently, the Itanium C++ ABI stores no array cookie when the element type is trivially destructible and has no two-argument class-scope operator delete[], which is Clang's rule as well. The design already requires trivial destruction of the block (design.txt:328) but does not connect that requirement to the array form, and it does not ask for a static_assert on the trait or a check that the arena byte count is a whole number of blocks.

Words used here: array placement-new = the C++ form ::new (p) T[n] that creates n objects at an address p that is already allocated. Array cookie = a hidden element count a compiler may store in front of such an array. kv_block = the struct holding one KV head's K and V data for one page. The same linked page prescribes, in its own "Recommended edits" item 7, exactly the design's form: "Replace 'placement construction' with the exact form: ::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[n_kv_heads * n_pages]; per storage slot region, no parentheses or braces" [prior-review.txt:1794]. Round-1 F12's recommendation on the same page also offers ::new (region_base) kv_block_t[n_kv_heads * n_pages]; as an accepted alternative [prior-review.txt:459-463; r1-findings.md F12 Recommendation]. The warning the finding quotes is one verifier's refinement 3(b) on the votes sub-page (status/claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-votes.html#C09, reached from the C09 entry's "votes and corrections" link) and in r1-findings.md, which the design does not link. The round-1 lead's synthesis did not adopt that refinement. So the design followed the linked page's instruction; an implementing agent reading the design and its linked page sees one form, not two. The disposition row "F12 F40 F56 C01 C09 | Accepted; array extent clarified" [design.txt:468] matches what the design took from C09: the per-slot extent and loop [design.txt:331-333]. 2. The finding's technical basis holds (this part is not refuted). With g++ 11.4.0 at -std=gnu++2b -O2 (the only compiler on this host; the pinned clang 19 is not installed here), ::new (p) T[n] for a trivially destructible T returns p with offset 0 (xorl %eax,%eax; ret), emits no memset and no loop, and returns offset 0 even for a type with a user-declared destructor; the only extra code is the bad_array_new_length bound check. That matches the C++20 exemption for the library operator new[](std::size_t, void*) (CWG 2382) and the Itanium ABI no-cookie rule for that placement form. I could not run the pinned clang 19; Clang's code generation also skips the cookie for the reserved global placement operator new[], but that is from memory of Clang's source, not tested here. 3. Sub-claim "does not ask for a static_assert on the trait" is partly wrong. The design requires trivial default construction, copyability and destruction for owner and block [design.txt:328] and asks the t_llama_unit test row to "Check block size/offset/alignment contracts and trivial type traits" [design.txt:399]. Only the placement of the check (next to the construction rather than in a test) is unstated. 4. Sub-claim "does not ask for a check that the arena byte count is a whole number of blocks" asks for a tautology. make_kv_slot_offsets computes block_bytes = KV_BLOCK_PLANES_2 * 64 * sizeof(bf16) * head_size and slot_bytes = n_kv_heads * block_bytes with checked multiplies [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:651-667]; block_bytes equals sizeof(kv_block<64, head_size>) by the existing static_assert [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1316-1318]; the arena byte count is n_pages times the per-page unit [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1165-1167]. For uniform geometry every slot has the same head_size, so the arena byte count is a multiple of sizeof(kv_block_t) by construction. The design's "checked arena byte count divided by sizeof(kv_block_t)" [design.txt:331] is therefore exact. AGENTS.md discourages assertions derived from the same data under test [AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:39-41]. 5. Other cited facts check out: kv_block holds only bf16s arrays [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2190-2202]; bf16x8/bf16x16 are __m128i/__m256i aliases [h/tron/simd/types.hpp@2880c3aa9b:25-27]; allocate_kv_group has no divisibility check [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1199-1208]; the design says "Verify the construction form with the pinned compiler" [design.txt:337].

That HTML file contains the string "unspecified extra bytes" zero times and the word "Verifier correction" zero times (grep -c on the file, 231,363 bytes, 2026-09-21 19:46). Its rendered C09 entry (claim, evidence, recommendation) says "default-construct kv_block<page_size, spec.geometry.head_size>[n_kv_heads * n_pages] at arena + n_pages * byte_offset" and nothing against the array form [prior-review.txt:1465-1486]. The warning "(b) 'default-construct kv_block<...>[n]' should not be implemented as array placement-new (new (p) T[n]), which may consume unspecified extra bytes" exists only on the votes sub-page (claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-votes.html#C09, reached through the entry's "votes and corrections" link) and in the reviewers' scratchpad r1-findings.md. It is an unadopted verifier remark, not the round-1 recommendation. 2. The linked round-1 page's adopted guidance prescribes the array form. Its consolidated recommendation #7 reads: "Replace 'placement construction' with the exact form: ::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[n_kv_heads * n_pages]; per storage slot region, no parentheses or braces" [prior-review.txt:1794]. The F12 recommendation on the same page offers "::new (region_base) kv_block_t[n_kv_heads * n_pages]; per (arena, geometry) region" [prior-review.txt:459]. Two F12 verifier corrections on the votes page also endorse "::new (p) kv_block_t[n]; per region" (votes page text at chars ~98039 and ~102357). The design followed that guidance and cites [F12] [F40] next to the rule (design.txt:329). The [C09] cite at design.txt:333 is attached to the EAGLE-slot sentence, not to the construction form. So "the design gives no basis for overriding that warning" is wrong: its basis is the retained F12 recommendation it cites, and an agent reading the design plus the linked page has nothing to guess about. 3. The form is standard-guaranteed, as the finding itself concedes ("that form is correct"). C++20 and later ([expr.new], CWG 2382) allow array allocation overhead only when "the allocation function is not a non-allocating form"; ::new (void*) T[n] selects the library operator new[](std::size_t, void*), the non-allocating form. The repository builds with CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23 (facts-r2.md, Toolchain). Whichever way an implementer resolved the two-hop inconsistency, the result is correct: the array form and a per-element loop of ::new (p+i) kv_block_t; both default-initialize a trivially default constructible block and emit no clearing code. Ben's requirements in comment #3 ("The page arena must construct the actual storage type", no cast of an existing SIMD array, no "implicit clearing to hot allocation paths"; facts-r1.md:29) are met by either. No wrong build and no acceptance risk follow. 4. The two requested checks add nothing the design lacks in substance. (a) Trait check: design.txt:328 requires trivial default construction, copy, and destruction for owner and block, and the t_llama_unit row says "Check block size/offset/alignment contracts and trivial type traits" [design.txt:399]; whether that is spelled static_assert or a test assertion is taste. (b) Divisibility: bytes passed to allocate_kv_group is n_pages * sum over slots of (geometry.n_kv_heads * block_bytes), with block_bytes = KV_BLOCK_PLANES_2 * 64 * sizeof(bf16) * head_size [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:650-672, 1161-1167], and sizeof(kv_block_t) == that product by static_assert [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1316-1318]. So bytes % sizeof(kv_block_t) == 0 holds by construction for the uniform case, and the heterogeneous case constructs geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages blocks per slot without dividing [design.txt:332]. The proposed TRON_ASSERT cannot fail on a conforming build. Same for R36's "TRON_ASSERT that the returned pointer equals region_base": under the C++20 rule it is a tautology. Verified finding-evidence lines that do hold: kv_block holds only bf16s arrays [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2190-2205]; bf16x8/bf16x16 are __m128i/__m256i [h/tron/simd/types.hpp@2880c3aa9b:25-26]; the static_asserts at 1318-1319 cover size and alignment only; allocate_kv_group at 1199-1208 has no divisibility check. None of these change the verdict.
    Correction: What survives is a note, not an ambiguity: the round-1 review corpus is internally inconsistent two links away from the design (votes sub-page C09 correction (b) versus the round-1 page's recommendation #7 and the F12 corrections). The design may optionally add one sentence after the code block at design.txt:326: "C++20 [expr.new] (CWG 2382) forbids array allocation overhead when the new-expression uses the library operator new[](std::size_t, void*), so the first block starts exactly at region_base." No static_assert or TRON_ASSERT is required; the trait check is already in the t_llama_unit row (design.txt:399) and the byte count is a whole number of blocks by construction (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:650-672, 1161-1167, 1318).

Rejected N54. Retarget #4424 after pushing rebuilt branch, not before

Candidate claim: Ambiguity in sequencing: step 1 changes #4424's GitHub base to the parent branch while steps 2-3 still describe rebuilding the child history. Until the rebuilt branch is pushed, the PR diff shows the old child head against the parent branch, which includes the parent's changes reversed. The gh syntax itself is valid.

  • source lens: refuted (high confidence, severity note). The finding's mechanism is a factual error about GitHub pull-request diffs, and its recommended reorder would create the mixed-diff window that round-1 F14 warned about. (1) The finding says that after gh pr edit 4424 --base <parent-branch> and before the rebuilt branch is pushed, "the PR diff shows the old child head against the parent branch, which includes the parent's changes reversed". That describes a two-dot diff (parent..child). GitHub's Files-changed view is a three-dot diff (merge-base...head). GitHub's own reference page says: "Pull requests on GitHub show a three-dot diff" and "the three-dot comparison uses the merge base, it focuses on 'what a pull request introduces'" [https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/branches, section "Three-dot and two-dot Git diff comparisons"]. (2) Live data confirms this for PR 4424 itself. git merge-base 2880c3aa9b 30c4ac82cbb6 = c7844ca2ce. Three-dot git diff --stat 2880c3aa9b...30c4ac82cbb6 = 25 files, +2082/-145. Two-dot git diff --stat 2880c3aa9b..30c4ac82cbb6 = 119 files, +5230/-8410 (it includes main's changes reversed, e.g. bin/ci/benchmark_lib.py, a file the child never touched). gh pr view 4424 --json changedFiles,additions,deletions returns 25 / 2082 / 145, although main has moved from the recorded baseRefOid f46e48ba to 2880c3aa9b. So GitHub already shows the three-dot form today. (3) The parent branch starts "on a fresh branch from fetched main" [design.txt:352], so merge-base(parent-branch, 30c4ac82cb) stays c7844ca2ce. Retargeting the base to the parent branch before pushing the rebuilt child therefore leaves the Files-changed view unchanged (still the child's 25 files). The only interim effect is the mergeability indicator showing conflicts (round-1 F15 measured one textual conflict in common.hpp against 98bb8cb2), which is harmless on a draft PR; the design already says "Keep it draft" [design.txt:366]. (4) The finding's recommended order (push the rebuilt jhan-amx-vnniK first, then retarget) is the harmful one. A rebuilt child = parent commits + child commits. With base still main, merge-base(main, rebuilt) is the main commit the parent forked from, so the three-dot diff would show the parent's commits inside #4424's Files-changed view. That is exactly the "diff will show the parent's commits as well as its own" problem round-1 F14 raised [r1-findings.md, F14 Claim], which the design's step 1 [design.txt:366] fixes by retargeting first. (5) The recommendation's other part, "preserve the old head (tag or branch)", is already in the design: "Preserve the old child head locally before replacing any branch history" [design.txt:364]. (6) What the finding gets right: step 1 does precede the rebuild steps 2-3 [design.txt:366-368], and the gh pr edit --base syntax is valid (gh pr edit --help line 27: "-B, --base branch Change the base branch for this pull request"). Neither is a defect.
    Correction: Corrected claim (note, no change required): between step 1 (retarget #4424's base to the parent branch) and the push of the rebuilt child, #4424's Files-changed view stays the child-only three-dot diff (25 files vs merge-base c7844ca2ce) and only the mergeability indicator reports conflicts, which is acceptable on a draft. Retargeting before pushing is the correct order; pushing the rebuilt branch first would make #4424 show the parent's commits against main, the F14 problem.
